EDCS-00380245.translation: Quarta Iovonia Tertia, daughter of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, and Salvius Cocceius, son of Gaius, erected [this monument].
EDCS-00380245.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Quarta Iovonia Tertia and Salvius Cocceius, likely as a family tombstone.

EDCS-00380248.translation: Gaius Genucius, son of Gaius, duovir and aedile; Otatia Tertia, daughter of Publius, his wife; and Gaius Genucius, son of Gaius, [his] son and duovir and aedile.
EDCS-00380248.summary: This inscription records members of the Genucius family, likely on a public monument, identifying Gaius Genucius and his son as duovirs and aediles.

EDCS-02900273.summary: This is a simple tombstone for Vennonia Prima, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-03000329.translation: To Lucius Herennius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-03000329.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating a monument or tomb to Lucius Herennius.

EDCS-03000331.translation: Gaius Nevius Asus, son of Gaius, of the Voltinia tribe, of the legion IV.
EDCS-03000331.summary: This inscription records Gaius Nevius Asus, a soldier of the Legio IV, identified by his name, father, and tribe.

EDCS-03300213.summary: This is a simple inscription of a name, Gnaeus Ateius, possibly on a tomb or marker.

EDCS-03300214.summary: This inscription records Eros, identified as belonging to Gnaeus Ateius, likely a freedman or slave on a tombstone.

EDCS-03300215.summary: This inscription records Sabinus, identified as belonging to Gnaeus Ateius, likely a freedman or slave on a tombstone.

EDCS-03300216.summary: This inscription records Zoilus, identified as belonging to Gnaeus Ateius, likely a freedman or slave on a tombstone.

EDCS-03300223.summary: This is a simple inscription of a name, Lucius Gellius, possibly on a tomb or marker.

EDCS-03300225.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the names Quintus L. E.

EDCS-03300227.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Gaius Murrius Primigenius.

EDCS-03300229.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the names Gaius P. P.

EDCS-03300230.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Passius Telamo.

EDCS-03300231.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Marcus Perennius Crescens.

EDCS-03300236.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Lucius Rufius Acer.

EDCS-03300239.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Gaius Sertorius Ocella.

EDCS-03300240.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Quintus Sertorius.

EDCS-03300241.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the name Aulus Sestius Dama.

EDCS-03300243.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription giving the names Gaius T. A.

EDCS-03300244.translation: Festus, son of C., of tribe T.
EDCS-03300244.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming a person and their tribal affiliation.

EDCS-03300245.translation: Gaius, son of T., of tribe P.
EDCS-03300245.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely naming a person and their tribal affiliation.

EDCS-03300252.summary: This inscription simply names two individuals, Salvetus and Vitalis.

EDCS-03300255.translation: Vertius Niger, son of Spurius, of the Pollia tribe, 40 years old; Gaius Vertius, son of Niger, 5 years old.
EDCS-03300255.summary: This funerary inscription records two individuals, likely father and son, noting their names, parentage, tribal affiliation, and ages.

EDCS-03300259.translation: [3] Caelius, son of Marcus, of the Publilia tribe, to Calvisio.
EDCS-03300259.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be a dedication from Caelius to Calvisio.

EDCS-03300261.translation: AM[3], son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, Optatus
EDCS-03300261.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription naming an individual, possibly Optatus, with patronymic and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-03300264.translation: To the departed spirits; Nonieca, daughter of MEI[3], a virgin.
EDCS-03300264.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Nonieca, identified as a virgin daughter.

EDCS-03700268.translation: To the departed spirits; Cn. Attius Iulianus(?).
EDCS-03700268.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription dedicated to Cn. Attius Iulianus(?).

EDCS-03700271.summary: This inscription records the name Vireia Secunda and her father Marcus.

EDCS-03700272.translation: Titus Lucius, son of Valerius(?), son of Caius(?).
EDCS-03700272.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription providing names and likely patronymics or filiation for two individuals.

EDCS-03700273.translation: Sextus Messius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, and Veltavia, and Sextus Messius, son of Sextus, of the Camilia tribe, and Maxsumus, and Vibia Polla, daughter of Titus, his wife.
EDCS-03700273.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing several members of the Messius family, likely on a tombstone.

EDCS-03700274.translation: To Mantia Prisca, daughter of Gaius, to her brother Mantis, son [of X], and [to her] son [X].
EDCS-03700274.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to a woman named Mantia Prisca for her brother and son.

EDCS-03700275.translation: Gaius Antonius Quintellus(?), of the Camilia tribe.
EDCS-03700275.summary: This inscription identifies Gaius Antonius Quintellus, a member of the Camilia tribe, possibly on a public monument or tombstone.

EDCS-03700278.translation: In the consulship of Opilio(?), a most distinguished man, under the manager Sabinus, the conductor.
EDCS-03700278.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records a public work or contract during the consulship of Opilio.

EDCS-04900310.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aemilius Secundinus made this for Aemilius Thelonicus because of his merits.
EDCS-04900310.summary: This funerary inscription records Aemilius Secundinus setting up a monument for Aemilius Thelonicus due to his services.

EDCS-04900315.translation: To the Divine Shades. Iulia Fuscina made this for her most cherished husband, Flavius Lucretianus.
EDCS-04900315.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Iulia Fuscina for her beloved husband, Flavius Lucretianus.

EDCS-04900318.summary: This is a very brief funerary inscription dedicated to Licinia Amoena.

EDCS-04900322.translation: To Novicia [X], to her deserving husband Sextus(?) S() Ianuarius.
EDCS-04900322.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Novicia and her deserving husband, Sextus(?) Ianuarius.

EDCS-04900324.translation: To the Divine Shades. To Sextilia Patern(a), his most dutiful wife, who lived 29 years, 3 months, 5 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-04900324.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sextilia Patern(a), detailing her lifespan and expressing the grief of her husband.

EDCS-04900648.summary: This inscription appears to be a misreading or a non-standard text, possibly a graffito or a very informal marker.

EDCS-05000261.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Volta Tatia, a freedwoman, likely from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05000266.translation: To Mercury Augustus. Quintus Salvius Germanicus willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05000266.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mercury Augustus by Quintus Salvius Germanicus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05000269.translation: Marcus Cotius, son of Tertius, made this for himself and his family while alive.
EDCS-05000269.summary: This is an epitaph for Marcus Cotius, son of Tertius, who commissioned his own tomb and that of his family during his lifetime, probably from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05200230.text_edition: \n Titus Voconius Titi filius Iucundus vixit annos XV\n
EDCS-05200230.translation: Titus Voconius Iucundus, son of Titus, lived for 15 years.
EDCS-05200230.summary: This is a funerary epitaph recording the lifespan of Titus Voconius Iucundus, son of Titus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200232.summary: This is a very brief inscription recording that someone named Sanctus made something, possibly a building or monument, with the date and context unclear.

EDCS-05200240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Antonia Isias, a freedwoman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200241.translation: Lucius Flavius Primigenius, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-05200241.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Flavius Primigenius, a freedman, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200242.text_edition: \n Marcus Mallonius Lalus sibi et suis et Aureliae Synemnae sic uxori vivus fecit\n
EDCS-05200242.translation: Marcus Mallonius Lalus made this for himself, his family, and his wife Aurelia Synemna, while alive.
EDCS-05200242.summary: This epitaph records Marcus Mallonius Lalus commissioning his own tomb and that of his family, including his wife Aurelia Synemna, during his lifetime, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05200243.summary: This inscription records that Marcus Plautius Latianus commissioned something, likely a building or monument, possibly from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05400395.translation: For the genius of Marcus Cassius. Marcus Satrius Vitulus, his heir, took care of this.
EDCS-05400395.summary: This inscription is a dedication to the genius of Marcus Cassius, arranged by his heir Marcus Satrius Vitulus, likely from the Imperial period.

EDCS-05400396.translation: To the spirit of our Merops, Trophimus his slave.
EDCS-05400396.summary: A dedication to the genius Meropis by his slave Trophimus.

EDCS-05400409.translation: To Marcus Cocceius Severus, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, first-rank centurion of the Ninth Spanish Legion, prefect of the Tenth Gemina Legion. Cinnamus his freedman.
EDCS-05400409.summary: A dedication to Marcus Cocceius Severus, a military officer, by his freedman Cinnamus.

EDCS-05400410.translation: Marcus Coelius Clemens, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe, soldier of the 6th Praetorian cohort, aide-major, recalled soldier of the emperor, centurion of the IIII Flavia Felix Legion in Upper Moesia. He ordered this altar to be made for his parents and relatives in his will, and Gaius Petronius Firmus saw to its construction. Gaius Pompeius wrote.
EDCS-05400410.summary: A funerary monument with an altar dedicated to parents and relatives by a soldier, with the work overseen by a patron and inscribed by a scribe.

EDCS-05400426.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Attius Primae libertus Peregrinus sibi et Attiae Primae patronae Iuliae Primigeniae uxori Attiae Severae matri Attiae Peregrinae sorori Marco Iulio Philocali liberto Primigenio\n
EDCS-05400426.translation: Peregrinus, a freedman of Attius Prima, made this while alive for himself, for his patroness Attia Prima, for his wife Iulia Primigenia, for his mother Attia Severa, for his sister Attia Peregrina, and for his freedman Primigenius.
EDCS-05400426.summary: A funerary dedication made by a freedman for himself and his family, including his patroness.

EDCS-05400587.translation: Vennonius Clemens, son of Superus Victor, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05400587.summary: A votive dedication by Vennonius Clemens, son of Superus Victor.

EDCS-05400588.translation: Aemilius Monninus, son of Indutus Firmus. Monninus, son of Aemilius.
EDCS-05400588.summary: A simple statement of paternity for two individuals, Aemilius Monninus and Monninus Aemilius.

EDCS-05400589.translation: Titus Vettius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, aedile. Vettia Secunda, daughter of Titus, his wife, made this.
EDCS-05400589.summary: A dedication by Vettia Secunda, wife of Titus Vettius, who was an aedile.

EDCS-05400590.translation: Titus Moninus Tertius, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, a veteran. He ordered this to be made in his will for Titus Moninus Maxsimus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe, and for his wife Hospita, freedwoman of Pontia. In front 30 feet, in the field 20 feet.
EDCS-05400590.summary: A funerary monument commissioned in a will by a veteran, Titus Moninus Tertius, for his son and daughter-in-law, with dimensions specified.

EDCS-05400592.translation: To Blaesius, son of Cosaciacus Solici[---], Ter[---].
EDCS-05400592.summary: A fragmentary dedication to an individual named Blaesius.

EDCS-05400593.translation: Gaius Bruttius Vibius, son of Mani, of the Stellatina tribe. Bruimus, son of Gaius, of the Stellatina tribe.
EDCS-05400593.summary: A statement of paternity for two individuals, Gaius Bruttius Vibius and Bruimus, both from the Stellatina tribe.

EDCS-05400594.translation: Attia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, wife of the flamen of the divine Drusilla, gave a bathhouse and pool from her own property to her fellow townsfolk.
EDCS-05400594.summary: A funerary or honorific inscription from a woman who funded public amenities, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400595.translation: Quintus Mannius, son of Rufi, of the Stellatina tribe, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and his son Primo.
EDCS-05400595.summary: A funerary inscription for a man and his son, commissioned by will, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400596.translation: VIIVCI[---]IDI S P S / OP MVS O / Veioiatiac S / SCF Secunda / and for herself / P F F
EDCS-05400596.summary: An inscription of uncertain meaning, possibly funerary, with Latin and possibly Celtic elements, its date and purpose are unclear.

EDCS-05400597.summary: A fragment of an inscription, possibly funerary, that mentions personal names or kinship terms, with an unclear date and context.

EDCS-05400598.translation: To the spirits of the departed, Vera Blaionia set up this monument for her dearest husband Lucius Veltius Avitianus while she was still alive, with the help of her sons, including the title and the cuirass.
EDCS-05400598.summary: A funerary inscription set up by a wife for her husband, including a military item, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400609.translation: For Votio Davera, a virgin, a sarcophagus.
EDCS-05400609.summary: A funerary inscription for a young woman, identifying her as a virgin and specifying the monument as a sarcophagus, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400611.translation: To the Unconquered Sun God Mithras. [---] the Augustalis / [---], freedman / [---], freedman / [---], freedman / [---], son of Aulus / [
EDCS-05400611.summary: A dedication to the god Mithras, mentioning a high-ranking local official and several freedmen, likely dated to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400613.translation: To Silvanus, Gaius Secundus Hermes fulfills his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05400613.summary: A votive inscription to the god Silvanus, indicating the fulfillment of a vow, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400614.translation: Gaius Maius Verecundus gave and dedicated this gift in the name of Lucius Cassius Caesennianus.
EDCS-05400614.summary: A dedication of a gift or monument by an agent on behalf of another individual, likely dated to the 1st-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400615.translation: Aurelius Veteranus, a highly valued *beneficiarius* of the elite legion XIII Gemina, who lived 26 years, 7 months, and 15 days, Aurelius Secundianus, the *imaginifer* of the aforementioned legion, set up this memorial for his well-deserving cousin.
EDCS-05400615.summary: A funerary inscription for a soldier and his cousin who served in the same legion, likely dated to the 2nd-3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400616.translation: Aurelia Emerita lived 21 years, and Aurelia Ianuaria lived 4 years and 6 months. Aurelius Ianuarius, a standard-bearer of the 13th Legion, to his deserving wife and daughter. Aurelius Emeritus to his deserving daughter-in-law and granddaughter.
EDCS-05400616.summary: This funerary inscription records the deaths of Aurelia Emerita, Aurelia Ianuaria, Aurelia Emeritus's daughter-in-law, and Aurelia Emeritus's granddaughter, set up by Aurelius Ianuarius, a standard-bearer of the 13th Legion, and Aurelius Emeritus.

EDCS-05400617.translation: To the divine shades and perpetual happiness. Aurelius Quintianus, a surveyor of the 5th Macedonian Legion, to his dearest wife, Aurelia Vitellia, who lived 10 years [and...] R[...].
EDCS-05400617.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Aurelius Quintianus, a surveyor of the 5th Macedonian Legion, to his wife Aurelia Vitellia, who lived for an incomplete number of years.

EDCS-05400622.translation: To Gaius Marius Iulianus, an eques and flamen of Dertona, who lived 24 years and 7 months. Gaius Marius Aelianus, judge among the selected jurors from the V decuries, prefect of artisans (twice), duovir with judicial power in Vercellae, and flamen and pontifex of Dertona, decurion of Genoa, and father and flamen to his son and wife Iulia Thetis, erected this while alive for himself.
EDCS-05400622.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Gaius Marius Aelianus to his son and wife, commemorating the life and numerous public offices of Gaius Marius Iulianus, who died at a young age.

EDCS-05400624.translation: To Gaius Metilius Marcellinus, son of Gaius, of the Pomptina tribe, Roman eques, holding public equestrian rank, judge among the selected jurors from the V decuries, duovir quinquennalis, flamen of the deified Trajan, patron of all the collegia, patron of the colony of Forum Iulii Iriensium, and most faithful patron of the courts. The college of artisans of Dertona dedicated this to this most excellent and most abstinent man, citizen, for his outstanding innocence and loyalty towards individuals and the community collectively, by decree of the decurions, as patron, for his merits.
EDCS-05400624.summary: This inscription records the dedication by the college of artisans of Dertona to Gaius Metilius Marcellinus, honoring his many public offices, his roles as patron, and his virtuous character.

EDCS-05400626.translation: Gaius Curtius Valens, freedman, a builder.
EDCS-05400626.summary: This is a tombstone inscription identifying Gaius Curtius Valens, a freedman and builder.

EDCS-05400627.translation: Gaius Sulpicius Fusc[us], son of Lucius, of the Pomptina tribe, [in the trade of] clothier, [with a frontage] of 14 feet in front, [and a depth] of [...] feet in the land.
EDCS-05400627.summary: This inscription provides the name Gaius Sulpicius Fusc[us], his tribal affiliation, his profession as a clothier, and the dimensions of his property.

EDCS-05400628.translation: Severus, freedman, made this while alive for Marcus Petronius Quartus, son of Marcus, a clothier.
EDCS-05400628.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Severus, a freedman, for Marcus Petronius Quartus, a clothier.

EDCS-05400629.translation: To Publius Aelius Sabinus, who lived 24 years and 45 days. Antonia Thisipho, mother, to her most dutiful son.
EDCS-05400629.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Antonia Thisipho to her son Publius Aelius Sabinus, who died at the age of 24.

EDCS-05400630.translation: [...] Publius Arrius Viator, freedman of Publius. Publius Arrius Severus, [son of...] [is laid here]. In front 11 feet, in depth 10 feet.
EDCS-05400630.summary: This funerary inscription records the burial of Publius Arrius Viator, freedman of Publius, and Publius Arrius Severus, noting the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-05400631.translation: To Aurelia Lucia, dearest and most innocent woman, with whom [he] lived [for...] years.
EDCS-05400631.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Aurelia Lucia, praising her character and noting the duration of her relationship with the dedicator.

EDCS-05400632.translation: Aurelia Paulina placed this memorial for her daughter, who lived 14 years and 13 days.
EDCS-05400632.summary: A funerary monument set up by a mother for her deceased daughter.

EDCS-05400633.translation: Capitulatia Fidelis, freedwoman, for herself and Blesidia Prisca, daughter of Aulus; Aulus Felix, son of Salvius; Caesius Prima, freedwoman of Caius. In front 12 feet, in depth 14 feet.
EDCS-05400633.summary: A funerary plot inscription identifying the plot owner and dimensions, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400634.translation: Quartus Cominius, son of Caius, for himself and his wife Tertia Petronia, daughter of Marcus, and Lucius Cominius, son of Caius, and Caius Cominius, son of Caius, and their brothers, and their sister Tertia Cominia, and the freedmen Ampliatus and Felix.
EDCS-05400634.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing the individuals for whom the plot was intended, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400635.translation: Coriscus, son of the freedman of Egnatius Frontonis and Iulia Eutychus, rests here. He was 16 years old.
EDCS-05400635.summary: A funerary inscription for a young man named Coriscus, identifying his parents and their status as freedpersons.

EDCS-05400637.translation: Publius Latinius Primus, son of Publius, by his will ordered this to be made for himself and his mother Summia Secunda, daughter of Titus, and his father Publius Lepidus, son of Publius. In front 12 feet, in depth 14 feet.
EDCS-05400637.summary: A funerary monument inscription commissioned by will, detailing the plot dimensions and beneficiaries.

EDCS-05400638.translation: Manilia Victrix for her deserving husband.
EDCS-05400638.summary: A funerary epitaph dedicated by a wife to her husband.

EDCS-05400639.translation: Plot of Lucius Manlius Felix. In front 16 feet, in depth 18 feet. [---]
EDCS-05400639.summary: An inscription marking the dimensions of a burial plot belonging to Lucius Manlius Felix.

EDCS-05400640.translation: [---] of Vhvius. Maximus, son of [---]. Iuria P.F.P. [---] his wife. [---] O.P.P. [---] 30 feet.
EDCS-05400640.summary: A damaged funerary inscription that likely records dimensions and possibly names of individuals.

EDCS-05400641.translation: Caius Plinius Damophilus and Vibia Flora rest here.
EDCS-05400641.summary: A funerary inscription commemorating Caius Plinius Damophilus and Vibia Flora.

EDCS-05400642.translation: Decimus Rubrius Castus, son of Decimus, for himself and Rubria, daughter of Decimus. [---]
EDCS-05400642.summary: A funerary monument inscription detailing the owner and intended beneficiaries, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400643.translation: The plot of Lucius Tullius, son of Lucius, freedman Fidelis. In the front, 12 feet; in the depth, 14 feet.
EDCS-05400643.summary: This is a funerary land plot marker specifying dimensions for the burial space of a freedman named Fidelis.

EDCS-05400644.translation: To the shades below. Alfia Aphrodite, his wife, with whom he lived for 25 years, [set this up] out of devotion for Lucius Varius Plotus.
EDCS-05400644.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Varius Plotus, dedicated by his wife Alfia Aphrodite who lived with him for 25 years.

EDCS-05400645.translation: Publius Vassidius Cosmus ordered this to be placed by his will for himself and Vassidia Galene, and Publius Vassidius Nedimus, and Publius Vassidius Gelotus, and his wife Curtia Tertia.
EDCS-05400645.summary: This funerary inscription records Publius Vassidius Cosmus dedicating a monument for himself and other family members, including his wife Curtia Tertia.

EDCS-05400646.translation: Gaius Vettius, son of Gnaeus, for himself and Lucius Vettius [...]
EDCS-05400646.summary: A funerary inscription fragment, likely a dedication for Gaius Vettius and Lucius Vettius, with the original text being incomplete.

EDCS-05400653.translation: Of good memory. Aurelia Eusebia [made this memorial] for her dearest husband Cerellius Proculinus, a most perfect man, who lived 45 years, 9 months, and 5 days, and who lived with his wife for 23 years, against [his] wishes [is this memorial].
EDCS-05400653.summary: This funerary epitaph honors Aurelia Eusebia's husband, Cerellius Proculinus, a 'perfectissimus vir', providing details of his lifespan and marital duration.

EDCS-05400654.translation: Of good memory. Flavius Candidus made [this] for his praepositus and cleric Ulpius Candidus, a praiseworthy man, who lived 77 years, 5 months, and 15 days, and for his dearest mother Aurelia Valeria, and for Munatia Spica.
EDCS-05400654.summary: A funerary inscription by Flavius Candidus for his deceased father, Ulpius Candidus, and his mother, Aurelia Valeria, and Munatia Spica.

EDCS-05400657.translation: [...] Boethius the Younger, a most illustrious man, consul. Also rests in peace his granddaughter R() Claudia, who lived 2 years and 8 months, departed on the 14th day before the Kalends of November, Eutharicus, a most illustrious man, consul.
EDCS-05400657.summary: This fragmentary funerary inscription records the death dates and ages of two individuals, including a granddaughter named Claudia, and notes the consuls for two separate dates.

EDCS-05400660.translation: Of good memory. Flavia Roccasa rests in this place, who lived 22 years, 8 months, and 10 days. Florentinus placed [this] against [her] wishes.
EDCS-05400660.summary: A funerary epitaph for Flavia Roccasa, who lived 22 years, 8 months, and 10 days, dedicated by Florentinus.

EDCS-05400661.translation: Here rests the innocent Martinianus in peace, who lived 3 years [...]
EDCS-05400661.summary: A funerary inscription for a child named Martinianus, who died at the age of 3.

EDCS-05400662.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace Perseverandus, a reverend and penitent man, who lived in the world more or less 65 years. He departed on the 11th day before the Kalends of [---] Rustic, consul.
EDCS-05400662.summary: This epitaph honors Perseverandus, a 'reverendus' and 'penitens' man, who lived approximately 65 years, with his death date recorded during the consulship of Rustic.

EDCS-05400663.translation: To good memory; here rests in peace Proiecta, who lived about 55 years.
EDCS-05400663.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Proiecta, who lived about 55 years, dated by the invocation 'to good memory' and 'in peace' to the later Roman period.

EDCS-05400664.translation: To good memory; here rests in peace Sendephara, who lived about 30 years, departed on the Ides of January in the consulship of Basilius the Younger, vir clarissimus.
EDCS-05400664.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Sendephara, who lived about 30 years and died on January 13th, dated by the consul Basilius the Younger to the later Roman period.

EDCS-05400673.translation: To the Matronae; Gaius Trebius Nepos willingly and deservedly fulfills his vow.
EDCS-05400673.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Matronae by Gaius Trebius Nepos, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400675.translation: To Quintus Attius Priscus, son of Titus, of the Maecia tribe, as aedile, duumvir for five years, flamen of Augustus, pontifex, prefect of engineers, prefect of the I Cohort of Spaniards and the I Cohort of Montani and the I Cohort of Lusitanians, military tribune of the I Adjutrix Legion, honored with gifts by the Emperor Nerva Caesar Augustus for the Suebian War with a golden crown and a pure spear, prefect of the I Augusta Thracum cavalry, urban plebs.
EDCS-05400675.summary: This is a lengthy career inscription for Quintus Attius Priscus, detailing his various military and civic offices, including decorations received from Emperor Nerva, likely dating to the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05400676.translation: Fausta lies here, aged 45 years. Lucius Valerius Felix, centurion of the Cohort of Ligures, made this.
EDCS-05400676.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Fausta, aged 45, with the monument erected by Lucius Valerius Felix, a centurion, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400677.translation: Gaius Atilius Bradua, son of Gaius, made this at his own expense. He also paved the same forum with squared stone.
EDCS-05400677.summary: This is a dedication inscription by Gaius Atilius Bradua, who funded the construction and paving of a forum, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400678.translation: Gnaeus Atilius Serranus, son of Gnaeus, flamen of Augustus, patron of the college(?).
EDCS-05400678.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription identifying Gnaeus Atilius Serranus, a flamen of Augustus and likely a patron of a college, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400680.translation: To Gaius Catius Martialis, son of Lucius, of the Maecia tribe, scribe, who lived 18 years. To Lucius Catius Severus, son of Gaius, father. To Gaius Virius Fidus, son of Gaius, grandfather. To Muciae Quarta, daughter of Publius, grandmother. Gaius Lucretius Genialis, friend, had this made for himself and his wife Valeria. You who have read our names, fare well.
EDCS-05400680.summary: This is a funerary monument for multiple family members and a friend, Gaius Lucretius Genialis, who commissioned it, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400681.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to be funerary, possibly for an individual named Ampliatus, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400682.translation: Lucretius and Livia Julius Ennius, son, had this made for Verina.
EDCS-05400682.summary: This is a dedication or funerary inscription commissioned by Lucretius and Livia Julius Ennius for Verina, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400683.translation: To Publius Manlius, son of Publius, freedman [name missing].
EDCS-05400683.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedman, Publius Manlius, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400684.translation: To Gaius Octavius Obsequens and Prudens, to their mother.
EDCS-05400684.summary: This funerary dedication is from two sons, Gaius Octavius Obsequens and Prudens, to their mother.

EDCS-05400685.translation: Secunda had this made for her daughter.
EDCS-05400685.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Secunda for her daughter.

EDCS-05400686.translation: Titus Nonius Potitus erected [this] to Publius Valerius Primus, son of Publius, freedman.
EDCS-05400686.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Titus Nonius Potitus to Publius Valerius Primus, a freedman and likely a friend or associate.

EDCS-05400687.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Albia Aphrodisia, their mother, [erected] this tombstone to her most dutiful sons, Vettius Hermadion, who lived 16 years, 3 months, and Hermio, who lived 8 years, and Hermetis, who lived 7 years, who were snatched away from their mother by their humanity and the status of their piety.
EDCS-05400687.summary: This funerary epitaph, likely from the Roman Imperial period, is dedicated by Albia Aphrodisia to her three young sons who died prematurely.

EDCS-05400693.text_edition: \n Marco Vibio Quinti filio Pom(ptina) veterano legionis IX Hispaniensis Herenniae Marci filiae Salinae uxsori sic Salvio Vibio Marci filio Pom(ptina) Clementi\n
EDCS-05400693.translation: To Marcus Vibius, son of Quintus, of the Pomptina tribe, a veteran of the Ninth Spanish Legion; to Herennia Salina, daughter of Marcus, his wife; and to Salvius Vibius Clemens, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe.
EDCS-05400693.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Marcus Vibius, a veteran, his wife Herennia Salina, and their son Salvius Vibius Clemens.

EDCS-05400694.translation: The plot of land of Lucius Marcius Catiorum, son of Sextus, and of Terentia Secunda, daughter of Marcus, and of Titia Postuma, daughter of Lucius, and of Marcus Catius, son of Lucius. In front 45 feet, in the field 35 feet.
EDCS-05400694.summary: This is a boundary inscription defining the dimensions of a plot of land owned by several individuals, likely for burial or agricultural use.

EDCS-05400695.translation: Lucius Cornelius Solicius, son of Publius, of the Pomptina tribe, and Urvina Exsomna, daughter of Lucius, [made this] for their father Publius Cornelius Solicius, son of Publius, of the Pomptina tribe, and for their mother.
EDCS-05400695.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Cornelius Solicius and Urvina Exsomna for their parents.

EDCS-05400696.translation: Quintus Mettius Stabilio, son of Spurius, lived virtuously. Primmep.
EDCS-05400696.summary: This is a brief epitaph for Quintus Mettius Stabilio, indicating a virtuous life.

EDCS-05400698.translation: Marcus Vibius Homuncio, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, erected [this] for himself and his family to Marcus Vibius, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, his father; and to Trebia Posilla, daughter of Quintus, his mother; and to Lusia Vera, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-05400698.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Marcus Vibius Homuncio for himself and his family, honoring his parents and wife.

EDCS-05400699.translation: Eyafeus and Saerus, freedmen of Firmanus, and Rhenius the vilicus, have willingly and deservedly fulfilled their vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-05400699.summary: This is a votive inscription by freedmen and a vilicus dedicated to Jupiter, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400700.translation: To the spirits of Marcus Sullius Marcellus, son of Marcus, fourth official with curule authority, fourth official with judicial authority, quaestor, and his mother Marcia Severa, daughter of Victor, most dutiful parents. Marcus Sullius Verus, fourth official, ordered by his will that this be made, and he bequeathed 400 HS to the villagers of Iadatis, so that from its income they may place a rose for his parents and himself each year.
EDCS-05400700.summary: This is a funerary monument for Marcus Sullius Marcellus and his mother Marcia Severa, with a significant endowment to a local community for perpetual remembrance, likely dating to the 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05400701.translation: For Lucius Ursicus Boetus, freedman of Lucius, born in Asia, who rests here, and for his wife Suaefia Bassa, daughter of Lucius. Sextus Suaefius Celer, son of Sextus, of the Pollia tribe, and Gaius Suaefius Fuscus, son of Sextus, of the Pollia tribe, and his wife Suaefia Bassa, daughter of Lucius, have set up this monument for their heirs. And for Suaefia Bassa, daughter of Lucius, with 15 feet in front and 20 feet in the land.
EDCS-05400701.summary: This tomb inscription records the burial of Lucius Ursicus Boetus and his wife Suaefia Bassa, with further space allocated for Suaefia Faustae, and was erected by their heirs, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400702.translation: The guild of centonarii of Vardagates made this at their own expense for Gaius Avilius Severus and Avilia Severa, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-05400702.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by a guild for two individuals, Gaius Avilius Severus and Avilia Severa, likely dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400703.translation: To the spirits and memory of Simplicius, and Statilia Tigris, who lived 36 years. 'O most beautiful and always chaste, you lay on two marital couches, giving birth to two sons of love; had he been able to conquer fate, he would have placed this epitaph of praise for you. But I, unhappy, who lacked such a one, enjoyed sixteen years of your chastity and love.' Publius Vibius Verissimus, living, placed this for his incomparable wife and himself. Euphilus for Simplicius.
EDCS-05400703.summary: This epitaph commemorates Statilia Tigris, who died at 36, and includes a lengthy poetic tribute from her husband Publius Vibius Verissimus, who also erected it for himself and their son Simplicius, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400704.translation: Titus Vettius Hermes, freedman of Titus, a seller of perfumed oils, made this while alive. His mother gave birth to him, and his mother also received him. These gardens are as excellent and supreme as possible for my ashes. Serve them, for I will appoint caretakers, so that they may eat from the income of these gardens on my birthday and with roses in perpetuity. I do not wish these gardens either to be divided or alienated.
EDCS-05400704.summary: This is an endowment inscription by Titus Vettius Hermes, a perfumer, for the perpetual upkeep of his gardens and for the celebration of his birthday, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400705.translation: Irria Secunda, daughter of Salvius, for herself and for Gaius Sulpicius Severus, her husband, a vigintivir and Augustalis. [
EDCS-05400705.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Irria Secunda and her husband Gaius Sulpicius Severus, a prominent local official, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400706.translation: Publius Equinius Popita, son of Publius, of the Cominia tribe; his wife St(a)tia, daughter of Statius, of the Pollia tribe; Publius Equinius Ingenuos, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe; [--] Equinius, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, a sexvir.
EDCS-05400706.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of the Equinius family, including a sexvir, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400707.translation: Sacred to Neptune. Lucius Gessius Optatus willingly, joyfully, and deservedly.
EDCS-05400707.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Neptune by Lucius Gessius Optatus, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400708.translation: To Gaius Hirpidius Memor, son of Gaius, prefect of the artisans, judge from the list of ten decuries, military tribune of the III Augusta legion, prefect with judicial authority of Emperor Nerva Trajan Caesar Augustus Germanicus Dacicus, perpetual flamen, [patron of the deified Vespasian, the deified Nerva, and also the deified Trajan].
EDCS-05400708.summary: This is a dedication to Gaius Hirpidius Memor, listing his extensive career in military, judicial, and religious offices, likely from the late 1st or early 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05400709.translation: Lucius Accaedius Clemens paid his vow to Jupiter.
EDCS-05400709.summary: A votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Lucius Accaedius Clemens.

EDCS-05400710.translation: Lucius Cominius Cervicla, freedman of Lucius, and Lucius Cominius Fuscus, freedman of Lucius, gave willingly.
EDCS-05400710.summary: An inscription recording the donation by two freedmen, Lucius Cominius Cervicla and Lucius Cominius Fuscus.

EDCS-05400711.translation: Licinius Agatho willingly and deservedly (dedicated this) to Jupiter Best and Greatest.
EDCS-05400711.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Licinius Agatho.

EDCS-05400712.translation: Caius Fulvius Philologus, freedman of Caius, master of the Guild of Minerva, and his wife Pulfennia Sabina, daughter of Titus, and their son Caius Fulvius Sabinus, son of Caius.
EDCS-05400712.summary: An inscription commemorating a family group including Caius Fulvius Philologus, his wife Pulfennia Sabina, and their son Caius Fulvius Sabinus, with a reference to his magisterial role.

EDCS-05400713.translation: The brothers Vitalis Tertius, Quartus Firmus, sons of Lucius Marius, paid their vow to Mars willingly and joyfully.
EDCS-05400713.summary: A votive inscription to Mars by the brothers Vitalis Tertius and Quartus Firmus.

EDCS-05400714.translation: Titus Lollius Masculus, freedman of Titus, a high priest of the Bodincomagenses, was placed near the road so that passersby might say, 'Hail, Lollius'.
EDCS-05400714.summary: A funerary marker for Titus Lollius Masculus, a high priest, indicating his burial location near a road.

EDCS-05400715.translation: In the consulship of Caius Bruttus Praesens and Sextus Quintilius Condianus, Publius Popilius Priscinus, a seviri, erected (this monument) on his own land while alive; his sons and grandsons erected (monuments for) Publius Popilius Priscinus. Hail, greetings; may you fare well, whoever you are, traveler, and may he not fare well who moves me.
EDCS-05400715.summary: A funerary monument erected by Publius Popilius Priscinus and his descendants, with a strong inscription prohibiting its removal.

EDCS-05400716.translation: Sextus Octavius Cassianus, son of Sextus, of the Pollia tribe, was ordered by his will to be buried here. He lived 21 years.
EDCS-05400716.summary: A funerary inscription for Sextus Octavius Cassianus, detailing his age at death and his burial wishes expressed in his will.

EDCS-05400717.summary: An incomplete inscription, likely naming Caius Iulius.

EDCS-05400718.translation: Titus Grae() Trophimus, an Industrian, made (this) for Lucius Pompeius Herennianus, Roman knight, equo publico, quaestor of the public treasury, and aedile of the food supply, duovir, curator of the city treasury, and of the calendar for the Republic, as patron of the college of Industrian pastophori, because of his merits.
EDCS-05400718.summary: A dedication to Lucius Pompeius Herennianus by the college of pastophori of Industria, honoring his public service and patronage.

EDCS-05400719.translation: To the genius of Quintus Sertorius Synergus the younger, and to the genius of our patrons Quintus Sertorius Severus, by the industrious guild of craftsmen.
EDCS-05400719.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of two individuals and the patrons by a guild of craftsmen.

EDCS-05400721.translation: To our genius, by Moschus, slave.
EDCS-05400721.summary: This inscription is a dedication to a genius by a slave named Moschus.

EDCS-05400722.translation: To our Juno, by Quintus Lollius Eusebes and Acutia Prepusa.
EDCS-05400722.summary: This is a dedication to Juno by two individuals, Quintus Lollius Eusebes and Acutia Prepusa.

EDCS-05400723.translation: To Minerva, for the safety of Desticius Iubatus, a most distinguished man, and of Desticius Sallustius Iubatus, a most distinguished youth, and of their daughter Iubaea Sallustia Plotina, a most distinguished lady, Gallus, a slave and agent, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-05400723.summary: This is a votive inscription to Minerva, dedicating it for the safety of several members of the Iuba family, by their slave Gallus.

EDCS-05400724.translation: To the unconquered god Mithras, Gaius IndusTrius Verus gave this offering.
EDCS-05400724.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mithras by Gaius IndusTrius Verus, who presented an offering.

EDCS-05400728.translation: To Gaius Avilius Gallus, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, perpetual priest of the deified Caesar, patron of the municipality, tribune of the soldiers of the third Gallic legion, by decree of the decurions, being satisfied with this honor, he remitted the expense.
EDCS-05400728.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Gaius Avilius Gallus, recognizing his various public offices and patronage, with a remission of costs by decree of the decurions.

EDCS-05400729.translation: To Gaius Aulius Optatus, IIvir with aediciliary power, by Lucius Lucretius, son of Primi.
EDCS-05400729.summary: This is an honorary dedication to Gaius Aulius Optatus, a magistrate, by Lucius Lucretius.

EDCS-05400730.translation: Tertius Bresi, son of Autonis, a VIvir, and Minicia Stacia Iovinca, daughter of Stas, Salvius, a VIvir, and Marcus, a VIvir, his son, made this while alive.
EDCS-05400730.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Tertius Bresi and Minicia Stacia Iovinca, commemorating the builders (VIviri) Salvius and Marcus.

EDCS-05400731.translation: To Marcus Minis, son of Aulus, of the Pollia tribe, from the ten ancestral estates, first as a cavalry prefect, then as a quinquennial IIvir, a place was granted for the sake of honor, by decree of the decurions, he made this while alive for himself and for Minia Tertulla, daughter of Numerius, his wife.
EDCS-05400731.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Marcus Minis, recognizing his public offices, with a granted plot of land, made by himself for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05400734.translation: To Aulus Hostilius, son of Aulus, of the Papiria tribe, patron.
EDCS-05400734.summary: This is an honorary inscription for Aulus Hostilius, recognizing his status as patron.

EDCS-05400735.translation: To Gaius Lollius Agraulus, freedman of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, the guild of the *centonarii* (tent-makers), who, content with the honor, remitted the expense.
EDCS-05400735.summary: This inscription records a contribution by the guild of tent-makers to honor Gaius Lollius Agraulus, a freedman, who waived the costs associated with his office.

EDCS-05400736.translation: To Gaius Lollius Agraulus, freedman of Gaius, of the Palatine tribe, who was VIvir and Augustalis. Gaius Lollius Heliodorus [erected this] to his fellow guild-member.
EDCS-05400736.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription dedicated by Gaius Lollius Heliodorus to his fellow guild member, Gaius Lollius Agraulus, who held prestigious positions.

EDCS-05400738.summary: A simple votive inscription recording Avilia Amabilis fulfilling a vow, likely to a deity.

EDCS-05400739.translation: Lucius Fulfennius, son of Titus, for himself and for his sons Lucius Fulfennius Firminus, son of Lucius, and Lucius Fulfennius Secundus (?), son of Lucius, erected [this] while alive.
EDCS-05400739.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Fulfennius for himself and his sons, indicating it was prepared during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400741.translation: Gaius Papirius, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe; Cassia Fausta, freedwoman of Lucius; Papiria Prima, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-05400741.summary: This inscription lists names and tribal affiliations, possibly for a family tomb or an official record, with individuals identified by their patron or father and tribe.

EDCS-05400743.translation: To the Fountains (?) and to Diana Victoria, Titus Sextius Basiliscus, son of [?], of the Claudian Augustales, on his own behalf and for his wife Sextia Irenes, freedwoman of Titus, and for his son Titus Sextius Faustus, and for his daughter Sextia Marcella, fulfilled his vow willingly, gladly, deservedly on his own land within four boundary stones.
EDCS-05400743.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to deities by Titus Sextius Basiliscus, on behalf of his family, for a piece of land he owned.

EDCS-05400745.translation: Lucius Coelius, son of Quintus, soldier of the Ninth Legion, standard-bearer, honored for his valor with a *phalera* (breastplate ornament), torques (neck rings), and armillae (armbands).
EDCS-05400745.summary: This inscription honors Lucius Coelius, a soldier and standard-bearer in the Ninth Legion, for his bravery in battle, listing military decorations awarded to him.

EDCS-05400746.translation: To Titus Aebutius Leona, freedman of Titus, who was VIvir and Augustalis, and to Industria, daughter of I. Arreius, the honor was granted, the expense remitted.
EDCS-05400746.summary: This inscription records an honor granted to Titus Aebutius Leona and Industria, involving a remission of expenses, possibly related to public office.

EDCS-05400748.translation: Erected while alive. Lucius Vennonius Onesimus, freedman of a woman, who was VIvir Augustalis, for himself and [---]
EDCS-05400748.summary: This funerary monument was prepared during the lifetime of Lucius Vennonius Onesimus, a freedman and local official, for himself and at least one other person.

EDCS-05400749.translation: To the Spirits of the departed. For Marcus Albonius Callistinus, [and] for his most dutiful son Albonia Epagatho, and for Albonia Cale, his excellent patroness, and for himself.
EDCS-05400749.summary: This is a complex funerary inscription dedicated to Marcus Albonius Callistinus, his son, his patroness, and himself, set up for the deceased.

EDCS-05400750.translation: Cominia Pupa, daughter of Marcus, ordered this to be made by her will for her mother, Molota, and for Marcus Ennius Supero, son of Titus, and Titus Ennius Stabilio, son of Titus.
EDCS-05400750.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Republic or early Empire, commissioned by a woman named Cominia Pupa for her mother and two other individuals, possibly relatives or household members.

EDCS-05400751.translation: Valeria Aretusa, freedwoman of Caius, made this while alive for herself, her husband Gnaeus Pompeius Laevinus, son of Gnaeus (of the Quirina tribe), and her son Gnaeus Pompeius Laevinulus.
EDCS-05400751.summary: A funerary epitaph from Novaria, likely from the 1st century CE, set up by a freedwoman for herself and her family, including her husband and son, who held prominent positions.

EDCS-05400752.translation: Titus Vettius, son of Stalius, of the Pollia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will; Ennius and Catonia saw to its construction.
EDCS-05400752.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the late Republic or early Empire, commissioned by will by Titus Vettius and executed by Ennius and Catonia, possibly his heirs or agents.

EDCS-05400754.translation: Publius Vimivinus, son of Lucius, known as Clarus, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Dormino and Sueta.
EDCS-05400754.summary: An votive inscription, likely from the Imperial period, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Publius Vimivinus to deities or persons named Dormino and Sueta.

EDCS-05400755.text_edition: \n Genio patroni nostri Thallus Thallio Agathio liberti\n
EDCS-05400755.translation: To the spirit of our patron, Thallus, freedman of Thallius Agathio.
EDCS-05400755.summary: A dedication to the 'genius' of a patron, likely from the Imperial period, set up by his freedman Thallus.

EDCS-05400758.translation: Marcus Flavius Accius is buried here, a soldier of the XXII Legion.
EDCS-05400758.summary: A military tombstone, likely from the Imperial period, identifying the deceased as Marcus Flavius Accius, a soldier serving in the XXII Legion.

EDCS-05400759.translation: Pollia Marcella, daughter of Marcus, made this while alive for her father Marcus Pollio Certus, freedman of Marcus, and for her mother Aufidia Titulla, daughter of Titus, and for her brothers Lucius, Lucius, Titus, and Procula Vibullis, and for her husband Lucius Vibullius Montanus, a Six-member official of the Augustales of Flavialum.
EDCS-05400759.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, set up by a woman named Pollia Marcella for her parents, siblings, and husband, who held a prestigious local office.

EDCS-05400760.translation: To Marcus Valerius Crescent, son of Marcus (of the Tromentina tribe), Six-member official of the Augustales of Flavialum, and to his grandmother Baebia Tertia, daughter of Caius; Valeria Marcella, daughter of Marcus, set this up from her own resources.
EDCS-05400760.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, dedicated by Valeria Marcella to her father, who was a prominent local official, and her grandmother.

EDCS-05400761.translation: Caius Valerius Sceptus, freedman of a woman, Six-member official of the Augustales of Flavialum, made this while alive for himself and for his wife Vettia Romula, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05400761.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE, set up by a freedman and local official named Caius Valerius Sceptus for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05400762.translation: Marcus Coelius Mansuetus and Latinia Dextra and Procula, daughter, [set this up] for Vibius Asiaticus and Viria Sulpicia.
EDCS-05400762.summary: A funerary epitaph, likely from the early Imperial period, recording the erection of a monument by Marcus Coelius Mansuetus, Latinia Dextra, and Procula for Vibius Asiaticus and Viria Sulpicia, possibly family members.

EDCS-05400763.translation: To Gaius Vibius Asiaticus, son of Gaius. Lucius Aebutius Proculus [dedicated this].
EDCS-05400763.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius Aebutius Proculus to Gaius Vibius Asiaticus.

EDCS-05400764.translation: To the spirit of Asiaticus. Lucius Ennius Secundus and his sons Super and Tertius [dedicated this] to their best friend.
EDCS-05400764.summary: This is a dedication to the spirit of Asiaticus by Lucius Ennius Secundus and his sons, likely a funerary marker.

EDCS-05400767.translation: Marcus Octavius Optatus dedicated [this] at his own expense.
EDCS-05400767.summary: This is an inscription recording a dedication made by Marcus Octavius Optatus at his own expense, possibly for a public work or religious offering.

EDCS-05400768.translation: To Iulia Iusta, daughter of Gaius. Alypus, Terpusa, Nebris, Natalis, and Spatale, [her] freedmen [dedicated this].
EDCS-05400768.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Iulia Iusta, dedicated by her freedmen.

EDCS-05400769.translation: Lucius Livius Eurytus, freedman of a woman, made [this] while alive for himself and for Aebutia Adiutrix.
EDCS-05400769.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Livius Eurytus, made by himself while alive for himself and Aebutia Adiutrix, indicating it is a self-funded tomb.

EDCS-05400770.translation: To Lucius Mettius Varienus, son of Lucius and grandson of Statius, and to Rubria Secunda, daughter of Gaius, his wife. [She] made [this] for [herself] and her husband while alive.
EDCS-05400770.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Mettius Varienus and his wife Rubria Secunda, both of whom commissioned it during their lifetimes.

EDCS-05400771.translation: Petronia Grata, freedwoman of Lucius, ordered [this] to be made by testament for herself and for Petronia Grata, her mother, freedwoman of Lucius.
EDCS-05400771.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Petronia Grata and her mother, also named Petronia Grata, commissioned by the daughter through her will.

EDCS-05400772.translation: [Dedicated] to a friend. Prisca, daughter of Ter(---), wife [dedicated this].
EDCS-05400772.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly for a friend, dedicated by Prisca to her wife.

EDCS-05400773.translation: [He/She] made [this] while alive for [his/her] son Sex. [---] and for Secundus and for [---]umae. [Dimensions: frontage] 45 feet, [in the field] 35 feet.
EDCS-05400773.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for multiple individuals, commissioned by one of them while alive and indicating the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-05400774.translation: To the Divine Manes. For Septicia Sura. Lucius Petronius Melior [dedicated this].
EDCS-05400774.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Lucius Petronius Melior to the Divine Manes of Septicia Sura.

EDCS-05400775.translation: To Valeria Alete, freedwoman of Marcus, daughter of Spendia Moschis.
EDCS-05400775.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a freedwoman named Valeria Alete.

EDCS-05400776.translation: Caius Lucius made this for themselves and their family for Vesidia Tertia, daughter of Manius, and for Vesidia Rufa, daughter of Manius, mother of Mettia Comavi, daughter of Manius.
EDCS-05400776.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by Caius Lucius for themselves and their family, commemorating Vesidia Tertia and Vesidia Rufa.

EDCS-05400777.translation: To Publius Ulattius, son of Publius. His wife.
EDCS-05400777.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Publius Ulattius, set up by his wife.

EDCS-05400778.translation: [He was a] dignitary, bishop of Aquae. He died on the 7th day before the Kalends of February, during the consulship of Dinamius and Sifidius, most distinguished men.
EDCS-05400778.summary: This inscription records the death of a bishop of Aquae in the late Roman period.

EDCS-05400779.translation: Here lies in peace Maria of good memory, who lived in this world for 51 years and 11 months. She died on the 6th day before the Ides of January.
EDCS-05400779.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Maria, dating to the early Christian period.

EDCS-05400780.translation: Here lies in peace Desiderius of good memory, a count, who lived in this world for 40 years. He died on the 3rd day before the Nones of March, during the consulship of Aetius and Valerius, most distinguished men.
EDCS-05400780.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for Desiderius, a count, dating to the late Roman period.

EDCS-05400781.translation: Of good memory, here lies in peace Vigilia, an honorable girl, who lived in this world for approximately 18 years. She died on the Kalends of January, after the second consulship of Longinus and Faustus, most distinguished men, in the 15th indiction.
EDCS-05400781.summary: This is a Christian funerary epitaph for a young girl named Vigilia, dating to the late Roman period and including consular and indiction dating.

EDCS-05400782.summary: This is a dedication to the genius of Petronius.

EDCS-05400783.text_edition: \n Titus Calventius mulieris libertus Primitivus Papiria VIvir in suo vivus fecit\n
EDCS-05400783.translation: Titus Calventius Primitivus, freedman of a woman, a VIvir, made this for himself while alive.
EDCS-05400783.summary: This is an epitaph for Titus Calventius Primitivus, a VIvir and freedman, who dedicated his own tomb.

EDCS-05400784.translation: To Marcus Baebius, son of Publius, a veteran. To Lucretia Tertia, daughter of Caius. Publius Baebius, son of Marcus, the son.
EDCS-05400784.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Baebius and Lucretia Tertia, with Publius Baebius as the dedicator.

EDCS-05400785.translation: To Calpurnia, daughter of Publius, Rufa. Lucius Curtius Salvius, son of Spurius, [dedicated this] to his mother. Space in front, 12 feet.
EDCS-05400785.summary: A funerary dedication by Lucius Curtius Salvius to his mother Calpurnia Rufa, specifying the dimensions of the funerary plot.

EDCS-05400786.translation: [...]nia, daughter of Marcus, Oria; [...], freedwoman of Quintus, Iucunda, [hail?].
EDCS-05400786.summary: A fragmentary inscription that appears to record the names and filiations of at least two women, possibly in a funerary context.

EDCS-05400787.translation: To Marcus Cominius Secundus, son of Marcus, and to Terentia Clara, daughter of Primus, [their] sons Primus, Marcus, Caius, and also [to] Marcus Cominius Celer, son of Marcus, and Quintus Cominius, son of Marcus, their brothers, [erected this] monument, ordering [you] to grow up learning to return dutiful piety to yours.
EDCS-05400787.summary: A funerary monument erected by sons for their parents, Marcus Cominius Secundus and Terentia Clara, and for their brothers Marcus Cominius Celer and Quintus Cominius, with an admonition about filial piety.

EDCS-05400788.translation: To Marcus Cestius, son of Caius, and to Carantia, daughter of Marcus, Rufa, their sons Caius, Lucius, and Marcus erected [this].
EDCS-05400788.summary: A funerary inscription set up by three sons (Caius, Lucius, Marcus) for their parents, Marcus Cestius and Carantia Rufa.

EDCS-05400789.translation: To Plotia Prima, daughter of Marcus, who lived 13 years and was married for 100 days. Marcus Plotius, son of Caius, her father, and Egnatia, daughter of Marcus, her mother, erected [this].
EDCS-05400789.summary: A funerary epitaph for Plotia Prima, who died at 13 years old, erected by her parents.

EDCS-05400790.translation: To Marcus Calvisius, son of Marcus, of the Tromentina tribe, Veltovi, in accordance with his will.
EDCS-05400790.summary: A dedication to Marcus Calvisius, son of Marcus, of the Tromentina tribe, specifying that it was made according to his will.

EDCS-05400793.translation: To Marcus Ennius Germanus, son of Marcus, a veteran and patron, for his merits, and to his mother Vibía Fáusta, freedwoman of Quintus, and to his sister Ennia Quartá, daughter of Marcus, alive. Marcus Ennius Germanus, son of Marcus, erected [this] for himself while alive.
EDCS-05400793.summary: A funerary monument erected by Marcus Ennius Germanus for himself (as a living person), his deceased parents, and his living sister, honoring his status as a veteran and patron.

EDCS-05400794.translation: Quintus Licinius, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, aedile and quaestor, ordered [this] to be made by his will for himself and for his brothers Sextus and Publius, centurions of the VI Legion.
EDCS-05400794.summary: A funerary commission by Quintus Licinius, an official, for himself and his two brothers who were centurions in the VI Legion.

EDCS-05400795.translation: Publius Sertorius Tullus, freedman of Publius, his patron, a living Decurio, erected [this] while alive. Publius Sertorius Largus, freedman of Publius, a Decurio and Augustalis, [erected this] for Sertoria Severa, his wife, and for his freedmen Candido and Hermeto.
EDCS-05400795.summary: A funerary monument erected by Publius Sertorius Largus (a freedman, Decurio, and Augustalis) for his deceased wife Sertoria Severa and his freedmen Candido and Hermeto, and also commemorating his patron Publius Sertorius Tullus.

EDCS-05400796.translation: To Gaius Attius Livianus, son of Spurius, of the Tromentina tribe. [...], [erected] the stone.
EDCS-05400796.summary: A fragmentary funerary dedication to Gaius Attius Livianus, with the dedicator's name and relationship being lost.

EDCS-05400797.translation: To Lucius Caninius Valens, son of Publius, procurator four times of the publicani of Africa. Publius Caninius, son of Caius, his father, made this for himself and his son while alive.
EDCS-05400797.summary: A funerary monument erected by a father for himself and his son, who served as a procurator in Africa.

EDCS-05400798.summary: The beginning of an inscription mentioning Lucius Marius, with the rest of the text lost.

EDCS-05400799.translation: To Marcia Quarta, daughter of Lucius. Her parents made this.
EDCS-05400799.summary: A funerary monument erected by parents for their daughter, Marcia Quarta.

EDCS-05400800.translation: Vibius, son of Sextus, of the Camilia tribe, aged 28, killed...
EDCS-05400800.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vibius, son of Sextus, who died at the age of 28, likely in military service.

EDCS-05400801.translation: Lucius Didius Scaeva, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe. Attia Prima, daughter of Caius, his wife.
EDCS-05400801.summary: A funerary monument for Lucius Didius Scaeva and his wife Attia Prima, with the inscription indicating it was made by the husband while alive.

EDCS-05400802.translation: Titus? Cassius, son of Aulus, of the Camilia tribe, and Valeria Quarta, daughter of Marcus, his wife...
EDCS-05400802.summary: A funerary monument for Titus? Cassius and his wife Valeria Quarta, with the end of the inscription missing.

EDCS-05400803.translation: Sacred to...? Caius Mettius Verecundus, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, centurion of the Tenth Legion Gemina Pia Fidelis, gladly and deservedly gave.
EDCS-05400803.summary: A dedication made by Caius Mettius Verecundus, a centurion of Legio X Gemina, possibly to a deity or for a collegium.

EDCS-05400805.translation: To Concordia, from the college of artisans of Hastensium. Marcus Vettius Secundus, in memory of Vettia Civitas, his sister.
EDCS-05400805.summary: A dedication to the deity Concordia by Marcus Vettius Secundus on behalf of the college of artisans, in memory of his sister.

EDCS-05400807.translation: To Caius Stertinius Maximus, son of Marcus, decemvir for judging litigious cases, quaestor, tribune of the plebs, praetor, prefect of the military treasury...
EDCS-05400807.summary: An honorific inscription for Caius Stertinius Maximus, detailing his career progression through various magistracies and military appointments.

EDCS-05400808.translation: Gaius Arrius, son of Publius, veteran of the Thirteenth Legion Gemina, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for Baebia Ampliata, his wife.
EDCS-05400808.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by will by Gaius Arrius, a veteran of Legio XIII Gemina, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05400809.translation: Gaius Tillius Vitalis, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, veteran soldier, served in the 3rd legion for 32 years, as a *beneficiarius* of a tribune, for 21 years and 6 months.
EDCS-05400809.summary: This is a tombstone for a veteran soldier named Gaius Tillius Vitalis, detailing his military service.

EDCS-05400810.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Titus Solva Tiniani, son of Lucius, of the Flavia tribe, centurion of the 1st Adiutrix legion, centurion of the 3rd Augusta legion, centurion of the Gemini legion.
EDCS-05400810.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Titus Solva Tiniani, a centurion who served in multiple legions.

EDCS-05400811.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Ulpia Martina, his most loving wife, who lived 27 years and 7 months. Marcus Licinius Secundus, veteran former *optio* of the 14th Gemina legion, and Sabinilla and Viatorianus, to their most missed mother.
EDCS-05400811.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Marcus Licinius Secundus and his children to his deceased wife and their mother, Ulpia Martina.

EDCS-05400812.translation: Gaius Albius Ligus, son of Spurius, for himself and Curtia Clea, freedwoman of Gaius, his concubine, and Volusia Secundina.
EDCS-05400812.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Gaius Albius Ligus for himself and his concubine, and also for Volusia Secundina.

EDCS-05400813.translation: To Lucius Cantius Martianus, son of Lucius, of the public equestrian order, judge from five *decuriae*, *decurio* of Hasta and Aquileia, aged 27. Cantius Euhodus.
EDCS-05400813.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Lucius Cantius Martianus, a young man who held various civic and judicial positions.

EDCS-05400814.translation: Quintus Herennius Successor, *Vivir*, for himself and Herennius.
EDCS-05400814.summary: This funerary inscription records Quintus Herennius Successor setting up a tomb for himself and another individual named Herennius.

EDCS-05400815.translation: Publius Laetilius Hilarus Spuri, freedman of Publius, of the Palatina tribe, freedman of Minerva. // Naevia Almyris, freedwoman of the wife. // Clusia Topia, freedwoman of Gaius.
EDCS-05400815.summary: This inscription records the names of three freedmen: Publius Laetilius Hilarus Spuri, Naevia Almyris, and Clusia Topia, possibly related to a collegium or a family group.

EDCS-05400816.translation: To Lucius Pompeius Macer, son of Marcus, of the Pollia tribe, former *aedile*, *duovir* twice, *quinquennial duovir*, tribune of the soldiers of the people, (erected by) Herenniai, daughter of Lucius, his mother, Septumiae, daughter of Gaius, his grandmother. Aulus Hostilius Pompeius Macer.
EDCS-05400816.summary: This is a funerary monument dedicated by Aulus Hostilius Pompeius Macer to his father, mother, and grandmother, listing the father's public offices.

EDCS-05400817.translation: To Publius Vergilius Paullinus, son of Publius, grandson of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, *aedile*, *duovir* with the right to pronounce judgment, *prefect of the fabrica*, judge from four *decuriae*, an elector of the select cavalry, in public and private affairs, *prefect* of Drusus Caesar Germanicus' son, *quinquennial duovir*, (and to) Publius Vergilius Paullinus, son of Publius, grandson of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, with the public equestrian order, judge from four *decuriae*, *prefect of the fabrica*, *prefect* of the veteran 2nd cohort, of the army of [---].
EDCS-05400817.summary: This is a funerary inscription honouring Publius Vergilius Paullinus, a prominent figure who held numerous civic and military titles, with a section dedicated to a relative with similar honours.

EDCS-05400818.translation: Gaius Farronius Optatus, son of Gaius, a pack-bearer. Gaius Farronius Sabinus, son of Gaius, and Mactoria Ammia, wife of Lucius, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05400818.summary: This inscription lists two individuals named Gaius Farronius, likely father and son, and Mactoria Ammia, possibly the wife of the younger Gaius, with one identified as a pack-bearer.

EDCS-05400819.translation: Titus Valerius Placidus, son of Lucius, refector (a type of craftsman), son of Cornelia [---].
EDCS-05400819.summary: This inscription records a refector, Titus Valerius Placidus, son of Lucius, and mentions Cornelia.

EDCS-05400820.translation: To Titus Arrius Tertius, son of Titus, of the Tromentina tribe, aged 21. Mucia Modesta, daughter of Titus, his mother, made this for herself and for Titus Virulus, son of Marcus. Cruel fate snatched him away in his prime; it was not permitted for me, wretched man, to be above my husband. His father wept for his presence, his sisters wept, and his mother placed his bones in a warm pyre, she who previously should have read this inscription herself. 20 Roman feet in the ground, 20 Roman feet in the front.
EDCS-05400820.summary: This is a tombstone for Titus Arrius Tertius, who died at 21, set up by his mother, Mucia Modesta, and also intended for his husband, Titus Virulus, likely indicating a same-sex marriage. The inscription includes a lament for the deceased and specifies the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-05400821.translation: [---] Hilarus, freedman of Aulus, and Nymphis, freedwoman of Carrinatia, aged 17. 12 Roman feet in the front, 11 Roman feet in the ground.
EDCS-05400821.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Hilarus and Nymphis, freedmen, specifying plot dimensions.

EDCS-05400822.translation: Domitia Salvia, daughter of N[---], ordered this to be set up by her will for herself and for her son Luc[---].
EDCS-05400822.summary: This inscription records a burial arrangement made by testament by Domitia Salvia for herself and her son.

EDCS-05400823.translation: Gaius Fulvius Tarcussa, freedman of Gaius, father. For Gaius Fulvius Pacatus and Fidelis, sons. Fulvia Epicharis, freedwoman of Gaius, mother.
EDCS-05400823.summary: This inscription records a family, identifying Gaius Fulvius Tarcussa as the father, with sons Pacatus and Fidelis, and Fulvia Epicharis as the mother.

EDCS-05400824.translation: Marcus Petronius Primus, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will. Salvia, freedwoman, his wife, saw to its construction.
EDCS-05400824.summary: This inscription indicates that Marcus Petronius Primus arranged for his tomb by his will, and his freedwoman wife, Salvia, supervised its construction.

EDCS-05400825.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Bacchius set this up for Synoris, his freedman colleague and well-deserving wife.
EDCS-05400825.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Bacchius to his deceased wife Synoris, who was also his freedwoman colleague.

EDCS-05400826.translation: To Tituleia Flora, freedwoman of Aptius, mother. Quintus Tituleius Aptus and Atticus, sons, made this while alive and bought the plot. 12 Roman feet in the front, [---] Roman feet in the ground.
EDCS-05400826.summary: This funerary monument was erected by the sons Quintus Tituleius Aptus and Atticus for their mother, Tituleia Flora, who was a freedwoman.

EDCS-05400827.translation: Gaius Tullius Ingenius, son of Gaius, of the Pollia tribe, for his mother Cassia. [---] for his sister Tullia Iucunda [---].
EDCS-05400827.summary: This inscription is a dedication by Gaius Tullius Ingenius to his mother Cassia and his sister Tullia Iucunda.

EDCS-05400828.translation: Lucius Valerius Maxumus, son of Lucius. Gaius Valerius, son of Lucius. Two brothers [---].
EDCS-05400828.summary: This inscription records two brothers, Lucius Valerius Maxumus and Gaius Valerius, both sons of Lucius.

EDCS-05400829.translation: Viria Faventina, freedwoman of a man, ordered this to be made by the will of Caius Calsomirus.
EDCS-05400829.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by a freedwoman, Viria Faventina, at the behest of Caius Calsomirus.

EDCS-05400833.translation: Eusebia to her dearest son Eusebius, who lived 8 years, 10 months, and 8 days.
EDCS-05400833.summary: This is a tombstone for Eusebius, son of Eusebia, detailing his short lifespan.

EDCS-05400834.summary: This inscription, though incomplete, likely records the name Decima Pr[---]tia and possibly initials related to her status or the monument.

EDCS-05400835.translation: Quintus Valerius Optatus, freedman of Quintus, of the Palatina tribe.
EDCS-05400835.summary: This is a name inscription for Quintus Valerius Optatus, a freedman, indicating his tribal affiliation.

EDCS-05400836.translation: Lucius Pomponius erected this for Albinia Sympherusa while alive.
EDCS-05400836.summary: This inscription indicates that Lucius Pomponius erected a monument for Albinia Sympherusa during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400837.translation: Quintus Cominius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, lived 31 years[---].
EDCS-05400837.summary: This inscription records the name and lifespan of Quintus Cominius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-05400838.translation: Caius Aelius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will; Valeria Tertia, daughter of Sextus, his [wife?], saw to its construction.
EDCS-05400838.summary: This funerary inscription records Caius Aelius, who by his will commissioned a monument, and his wife Valeria Tertia, who supervised its construction.

EDCS-05400839.translation: Daughter dedicated to Atilia Maxsuma, daughter of Caius.
EDCS-05400839.summary: This inscription records a dedication made by a daughter to her mother, Atilia Maxsuma.

EDCS-05400840.translation: To the divine spirits. For Publius Aelius Marcianus, veteran of the II Parthica legion. Aelia Fuita to her incomparable husband, and Aelius Marcianus and Statinus to their well-deserving father.
EDCS-05400840.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Publius Aelius Marcianus, a veteran, by his wife and sons.

EDCS-05400841.translation: To Diana. Amandus, servant of Quintus Valerius Asiaticus, willingly paid his vow as deserved.
EDCS-05400841.summary: This is a votive inscription to Diana, dedicated by Amandus, a freedman of Quintus Valerius Asiaticus.

EDCS-05400842.translation: To the spirit of our Lucius, to our Clivana Juno, to our Annaea Juno. Vianellia Restituta (dedicates this).
EDCS-05400842.summary: This is a private dedication by Vianellia Restituta to household deities, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400843.translation: To Decimus Flavius Superus, son of Marcus, a soldier of the 8th Praetorian cohort, and to his wife Clementia, daughter of Quintus, and to his daughter Modesta, daughter of Publius. Decimus Flavius Fronto, son of Decimus, ordered this to be made in his will.
EDCS-05400843.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a son for his father (a Praetorian Guardsman), wife, and daughter, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400844.translation: To the departed spirits of Cominius Aelianus, an incomparable husband. Vequasia Plotiniana (dedicates this).
EDCS-05400844.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Cominius Aelianus, dedicated by his wife, Vequasia Plotiniana, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400845.translation: To the spirit of the guild of Albensian Pompeian Centonarii (transport workers). In memory of Salvius Cincius Semproniamus, an equestrian of Rome with public support, (his) mother Sempronia Sabina and (his) sister Iulia Sabina erected (this) at their own expense.
EDCS-05400845.summary: This is a memorial dedication by a mother and sister to a deceased member of the guild of Centonarii, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400846.translation: To the spirit of Gaius Petronius Rufus. (His) parents (dedicate this).
EDCS-05400846.summary: This is a dedication by parents to the spirit of their son, Gaius Petronius Rufus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400847.translation: Marcus Gavius Ligus, son of Gaius, willingly and gladly fulfilled (his) vow to Minerva.
EDCS-05400847.summary: This is a votive inscription recording the fulfillment of a vow to Minerva by Marcus Gavius Ligus, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400848.translation: To Tiberius Caesar, son of Drusus, grandson of Tiberius Augustus, great-grandson of the deified Augustus. Publius Varius Ligus, son of Publius, and (his) son (dedicate this).
EDCS-05400848.summary: This is an honorific inscription for Emperor Tiberius, set up by a father and son, likely from the early Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400849.translation: To Lucius Proius, son of Quintus, consul, praetor, plebeian aedile. The people of Emanenses (dedicate this) to their patron.
EDCS-05400849.summary: This is a dedication by the community of Emanenses to their patron, Lucius Proius, who held high offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400850.translation: Quintus Carrinas, son of Gaius, centurion of the first rank, twice aedile.
EDCS-05400850.summary: This is a dedication or epitaph for Quintus Carrinas, recording his military and municipal offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400851.translation: To himself and to his father Lucius Geminius Mancia, and to his mother Vibius Secunda. Manius Geminius, a veteran, son of Lucius.
EDCS-05400851.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a veteran, Manius Geminius, for himself, his father, and his mother, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400852.translation: To the shades of the underworld. Epaphroditus, freedman of Publius Atilius Nicostratus, a VIvir and Augustalis, set this up.
EDCS-05400852.summary: This funerary inscription honors Epaphroditus, freedman of Publius Atilius Nicostratus, who was a VIvir and Augustalis.

EDCS-05400853.translation: To Marcus Carsius Secundus, son of Manius, of the Camilia tribe, prefect of the military engineers, judge from five decuriae, curator.
EDCS-05400853.summary: This inscription honors Marcus Carsius Secundus, detailing his civic and military roles, including prefect of engineers and judge, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05400854.text_edition: \n Castriciae Saturninae filiae vixit nnos VI semissem Publius Castricius Saturninus pater magister Augustalis Pollentiae Augustae nnorum sibi et Mettiae Paulinae uxori optimae\n
EDCS-05400854.translation: To Castricia Saturnina, his daughter, who lived six and a half years. Publius Castricius Saturninus, her father, Augustalis magistrate of Pollentia Augusta, for himself and for his excellent wife, Mettia Paulina.
EDCS-05400854.summary: A funerary epitaph for Castricia Saturnina, a young girl, set up by her father, Publius Castricius Saturninus, an Augustalis in Pollentia Augusta, also for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05400855.translation: Erected by Gaius Cornelius Germanus, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe, while alive. He served as aedile, quaestor, duovir, prefect of the military engineers, judge from five decuriae, and flamen of the divine Augustus. For himself and for his excellent wife, Valeria Marcella, daughter of Marcus. He placed this himself in his own plot.
EDCS-05400855.summary: A self-funded funerary monument erected by Gaius Cornelius Germanus, who held various civic and religious offices, for himself and his wife, Valeria Marcella.

EDCS-05400856.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Lucius Didius Primus, aedile, quaestor, duovir, and for Messia Paezusa, his mother. Primi Didia Severina, freedwoman and wife, made this.
EDCS-05400856.summary: This funerary inscription records the monument made by Primi Didia Severina for her deceased husband, Lucius Didius Primus, and her mother-in-law, Messia Paezusa.

EDCS-05400857.translation: Gaius Fabricius Ligur, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, aedile, for himself and for his brother Marcus Fabricius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, also an aedile. His freedmen, Philetus and Fuscus, carried out the construction by his will.
EDCS-05400857.summary: This inscription records that a monument was commissioned by Gaius Fabricius Ligur for himself and his brother Marcus Fabricius, both aediles, and was executed by their freedmen.

EDCS-05400858.translation: For Gnaeus Iulius Pertinax, aedile, quaestor, prefect of the military engineers. Gnaeus Didius Hermes, for his most devoted son. The place was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05400858.summary: This inscription honors Gnaeus Iulius Pertinax for his public offices and states that the burial plot was granted by the local council (decurions).
