EDCS-05400859.translation: To the shades of the underworld. For Veiania Longina, for her most devoted husband, Gaius Lucilius Musa, a VIvir.
EDCS-05400859.summary: A funerary inscription dedicated by Veiania Longina to her husband, Gaius Lucilius Musa, who was a VIvir.

EDCS-05400860.translation: For Flavius Valerinus, his most devoted brother. His brother made this.
EDCS-05400860.summary: A funerary inscription by a brother for his deceased brother, Flavius Valerinus.

EDCS-05400861.summary: A simple inscription indicating the names of two slaves, Hermes and Elate, possibly on a tomb or marker.

EDCS-05400862.translation: Titus Mettius Pollio, son of Titus.
EDCS-05400862.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph for Titus Mettius Pollio, likely a tombstone inscription.

EDCS-05400863.translation: To Ulattius Elicinus, and Etocmus, comrade-in-arms of Ulattius Rufus, for their well-deserved merit, and for themselves.
EDCS-05400863.summary: This inscription is a dedication, possibly on a tomb or shrine, honoring Ulattius Elicinus and Etocmus, who were comrades-in-arms.

EDCS-05400866.translation: Marcus Livius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, brother of Sextus Livius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, Senecae, had this made. Sextus was a priest of the college of six (duumvir).
EDCS-05400866.summary: This funerary monument was commissioned by Marcus Livius for his brother Sextus Livius Senecae, who was a duumvir, likely in the late Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-05400869.translation: Titus Titius Felix, freedman of Titus, from the Pollia tribe, a native of Reate, I made this monument for myself while I was alive. This monument will not pass to an heir. In front, 12 feet; in the field...
EDCS-05400869.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument inscription, indicating the deceased Titus Titius Felix's desire for it not to be inherited, and it specifies the dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-05400870.translation: Lives Quintus Varisidius Naso, son of Quintus, of the Pollia tribe, a dyer. 16 feet in every direction.
EDCS-05400870.summary: This inscription records the burial plot size of Quintus Varisidius Naso, a dyer, indicating a square plot of 16 feet on each side.

EDCS-05400872.translation: Marcus Elvius Maximus for himself and for his wife Mettia Firmina, his father Marcus Elvius Cimbros, his mother Elvia Rufilla, his sister Elvia Fida, and his mother-in-law Didia Clementa. In front, 23 feet; in the field... This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-05400872.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Marcus Elvius Maximus and several family members, specifying plot dimensions and stating the monument is not to be inherited.

EDCS-05400873.translation: Marcus Galerius Philippus, freedman of Titus, erected this marker while alive for myself and my freedmen, before my marker.
EDCS-05400873.summary: This is a self-funded funerary monument inscription by Marcus Galerius Philippus, a freedman, indicating he erected it for himself and his freedmen during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400874.translation: Publius Cia[rtius?], freedman of Publius, Corinthus, for his mother Maecia Corinthis, freedwoman of Caius, and for Caius Maecius Secundus, freedman of Caius.
EDCS-05400874.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a monument to Maecia Corinthis and Caius Maecius Secundus, commissioned by Publius Corinthus.

EDCS-05400879.translation: Caius Mottius Celer, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his father Caius Mottius Rufus, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, for his mother Vettia Secunda, daughter of Lucius, for his brother Caius Mottius Maxumus, son of Caius, and for his sister Mottia Severa, daughter of Caius. Rufus Mottius Adiutor, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, from Ati[...]
EDCS-05400879.summary: This funerary inscription, ordered by will, dedicates a monument to Caius Mottius Celer and his family members, with a partial inscription for Rufus Mottius Adiutor.

EDCS-05400880.translation: Quintus Teielius and Vatia Siv[---] fulfilled their vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-05400880.summary: This inscription records the fulfillment of a vow by Quintus Teielius and Vatia Siv[---], likely at a shrine or religious site.

EDCS-05400881.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. Marcus Memmius Hermes, freedman, has paid his vow deservedly.
EDCS-05400881.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Jupiter by Marcus Memmius Hermes, a freedman, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-05400882.translation: To the divine spirit of Augusta. Valeria Epithusa, priestess.
EDCS-05400882.summary: This inscription honors the divine spirit of Augusta (likely an empress) and is set up by Valeria Epithusa, a priestess.

EDCS-05400884.translation: To Publius Titius Vilagenius, son of Gaius, of the Pollia tribe, for his father; and to Tertia, daughter of Lucius, for his mother.
EDCS-05400884.summary: This funerary inscription honors the parents of the dedicator, Publius Titius Vilagenius, a son of the Pollia tribe.

EDCS-05400885.translation: [Name]licus and Avilia Tertula, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05400885.summary: This inscription records the names of two individuals, [Name]licus and Avilia Tertula, likely a couple or related individuals.

EDCS-05400887.summary: This inscription records the name and position of Urbanus, who served as a steward or administrator.

EDCS-05400888.translation: Velta, wife, and Naevius Moctius, son of Aucius, and Secunda, daughter, made this while alive.
EDCS-05400888.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Velta, her husband Naevius Moctius, and their daughter Secunda, indicating it was erected during their lifetime.

EDCS-05400889.translation: The living souls condemn those crimes of earthly life they fear, the stains, rejoicing that they are freed from prison under Christ the judge, the powerful queen indeed seeks eternal dwelling after the chains of this age, and receives nothing of mortal death; these torches of virginity she kept in a chaste breast for your marriage-bed, Albinus, dedicated to the second [?] and nature’s loss that you, envious, do not grant children to your mother’s wishes, but willing to overcome with kind intention, and now has called forth offspring born of Albinus’s noble blood; hating the name nothing with great character [?] for the blessed mother’s heart.
EDCS-05400889.summary: This is a complex Christian funerary epigram commemorating a virtuous woman who remained a virgin and is now in a heavenly dwelling, praising her character and contrasting it with earthly suffering.

EDCS-05400890.translation: To Enica Comiogia, daughter of Nevius, lived. To Pramio, her husband, well deserving, with [her children?]. On the front [X] feet, in the field [Y] feet.
EDCS-05400890.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated to Enica Comiogia by her husband Pramio and possibly their children, also specifying the dimensions of the burial plot.

EDCS-05400891.translation: Ofillius Melior, freedman of Gracchus, of the Palatine tribe, as aedile, made this while alive. In front 40 feet, in the field 40 feet.
EDCS-05400891.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Ofillius Melior, a freedman and aedile, indicating the dimensions of his burial plot.

EDCS-05400892.translation: To the divine spirit of Victoria, Invictus, Emperor Caesar Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus, the unconquered leader. Eulalius, freedman, prefect of this station of the province(?) and of the sacred city(?).
EDCS-05400892.summary: This inscription is dedicated to the goddess Victoria and the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus Augustus by Eulalius, a freedman and prefect, likely in relation to a transportation or supply station.

EDCS-05400893.translation: Sacred to Victoria. Velti Setrixus and Avitus Paternus, with their families, have duly fulfilled their vow.
EDCS-05400893.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Victoria, recording the fulfillment of a vow by Velti Setrixus and Avitus Paternus.

EDCS-05400895.translation: Titus Fadius Pollentinus, son of Titus, freedman, as Augustalis magister, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-05400895.summary: This funerary inscription records that Titus Fadius Pollentinus, a freedman and Augustalis magister, commissioned his tomb by will.

EDCS-05400896.translation: Quintus Minicius Faber, who acquired this wealth from the beginning, made this for the eternal rest and memory of his wife Lollia Severa, his daughter Festi, and his sons Marcus Salvillus and Messorius. Publius Minicius Marmuris took care of it. In front, 50 feet; in the field, 50 feet.
EDCS-05400896.summary: This is a tombstone set up by Quintus Minicius Faber for his family, with dimensions indicating the plot size, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05400897.translation: Gnaeus Egnatius Iacula, son of Gnaeus, of the Fabia tribe, and his wife Considiena, daughter of Lucius, and their son Gnaeus Egnatius Iacula, son of Gnaeus.
EDCS-05400897.summary: This is a family inscription, likely a tombstone or monument, listing a father, mother, and son with their full names and tribal affiliations.

EDCS-05400898.translation: Quintus Flavius, son of Marcus, erected this.
EDCS-05400898.summary: A brief funerary inscription stating that Quintus Flavius, son of Marcus, set up the monument.

EDCS-05400899.summary: This is a simple dedication or funerary identification for Flavia, daughter of Mogetius.

EDCS-05400900.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Nevianius Saturnalus, son of Verus, of the Quirina tribe, who has served three times in office, made this while alive.
EDCS-05400900.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Nevianius Saturnalus, who had held public office three times, indicating it was made during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400901.summary: A fragmentary inscription that begins by identifying a man named Terentius, son of Marcus, likely part of a larger dedication or funerary text.

EDCS-05400902.translation: Lac(a)enus Bianius ORVIT(?) VI / F VIICO F VI / Lov CINPVOQVS decest F Mavius / decese vicus deceset / CILISA soror VI
EDCS-05400902.summary: This is a heavily damaged and difficult funerary inscription that appears to record the deaths of several individuals, possibly related, including Lac(a)enus Bianius, Mavius, and Cilisa.

EDCS-05400903.summary: A very fragmentary inscription, possibly a funerary dedication or epitaph, listing names that are difficult to fully interpret.

EDCS-05400904.translation: Salvia Verina, daughter of Lucius, made (this) for herself and for her most faithful husband, Sextus Catuesius Verus, son of Sextus, of the Pollia tribe, quaestor, duovir.
EDCS-05400904.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a wife for herself and her deceased husband, who held local magistracies.

EDCS-05400905.translation: Mocus Caranius, son of Nevius, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-05400905.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of an individual.

EDCS-05400906.translation: Marcus Cassius Marcellus, son of Marcus.
EDCS-05400906.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of an individual.

EDCS-05400907.translation: Sextus Livius Solo, son of Marcus, and his wife Seia.
EDCS-05400907.summary: This inscription records the names of a husband and wife.

EDCS-05400908.translation: Gaius Magilius Tertius, son of Gaius, of the Pollia tribe, from his will.
EDCS-05400908.summary: This inscription records the name and tribal affiliation of an individual, indicating the monument was erected according to his will.

EDCS-05400909.translation: Publius Modestus, freedman of Publius, made (this) dutifully for Publius Mallius Veranus, son of Titus, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-05400909.summary: This is a funerary epitaph set up by a freedman for his former master.

EDCS-05400910.translation: Tertius, son of Maximu, of the Pollia tribe.
EDCS-05400910.summary: This inscription records the name and parentage of an individual.

EDCS-05400911.translation: To Marcus Ammaeus, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, father; and to Prima, mother of Croprella.
EDCS-05400911.summary: This is a funerary epitaph honoring a father and a mother.

EDCS-05400913.summary: This inscription records the name of an individual who dedicated something.

EDCS-05400914.translation: Lucius [son of ---], Auma [son of ---], Po[---] sons of S[---].
EDCS-05400914.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording the names of several individuals, likely sons.

EDCS-05400915.translation: Quintus Virius Valens, alive, made this for his most devoted son Quintus Virius Superus and for himself and for his well-deserving wife Didia Procula. As was his duty as a son to his father, the father has erected this for his son.
EDCS-05400915.summary: A father erects a tomb for his son and his wife, indicating a son's filial duty as inspiration.

EDCS-05400916.translation: Maria Quarta, daughter of Caius, ordered by her will that this be made for herself and for her son Caius Albius Severus, son of Caius, a soldier of the Italian Legion, and for Publius Albius Secundus, son of Caius. Publius Albius Secundus, the son, who is also the heir, saw to its construction.
EDCS-05400916.summary: Maria Quarta's will dictates the construction of a tomb for herself and her two sons, one of whom, the heir, carried out the burial arrangements.

EDCS-05400918.text_edition: \n Caius Annius Cai filius Camilia Celer Augusta Bagiennorum testamento fieri iussit sibi et iliae Luci filiae Priscae matri \n
EDCS-05400918.translation: Caius Annius Celer, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, from Augusta Bagiennorum, ordered by his will that this be made for himself and for his daughter Prisca, daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-05400918.summary: Caius Annius Celer's will mandates the construction of a tomb for himself and his daughter.

EDCS-05400919.translation: Quintus Varius, the marble worker, alive, made this for himself and for his mother Viccia Polla, daughter of Publius; for his father Quintus Castricius Secundus, son of Marcus; for his brother Quintus Castricius Maximus, son of Quintus; and for his freedwoman Castricia Primigenia. Through the care of Marcus Cassius Severus, Augustalis. 36 feet in front, 46 feet in the area. This monument will not be inherited by an heir.
EDCS-05400919.summary: A marble worker, Quintus Varius, alive, commissioned a tomb for himself and several family members, including parents, brother, and a freedwoman, specifying dimensions and disinheriting future heirs.

EDCS-05400920.translation: [...son]etius, son of Titus, son of Pu[...]
EDCS-05400920.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely part of a funerary monument, with only partial names and filiations preserved.

EDCS-05400921.translation: Lucius Veianius Primigenius willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Hercules.
EDCS-05400921.summary: Lucius Veianius Primigenius willingly offers a votive dedication to Hercules.

EDCS-05400922.translation: Quintus Ennius Moccasus, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will; his heirs erected it for Moccasus Super and Feroxs.
EDCS-05400922.summary: Quintus Ennius Moccasus' will stipulated the construction of a tomb, which his heirs executed for Moccasus Super and Feroxs.

EDCS-05400923.translation: Catinia Cepria lived 17 years and took care to have this made by her will.
EDCS-05400923.summary: Catinia Cepria, who died at 17, arranged for a tomb to be built through her will.

EDCS-05400924.translation: Cassia Cyme, with her family, willingly, gladly, and deservedly fulfilled her vow.
EDCS-05400924.summary: Cassia Cyme and her family fulfill a votive offering.

EDCS-05400925.translation: Marcus Cassius Tenax, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, alive, made this for his father Titus Cassius Maxsimus, for his mother Mucıa Polla, daughter of Publius, for his wife Cassia Phyrallidi, and for his best friend Marcus Didius Phoebion, Augustalis, freedman of Marcus, and for his wife Ulattia Albanilla.
EDCS-05400925.summary: Marcus Cassius Tenax, alive, erected a monument for his father, mother, wife, best friend, and his friend's wife.

EDCS-05400926.translation: To the departed spirits. For Cassia Severa, daughter of Gaius, a most deserving woman, erected by Liberalissima, wife of Publius Catius Sabinus, and Speceia Secundilla, his mother, and for Gaius Cassius Hermadion, her freedman, a member of the VIviri.
EDCS-05400926.summary: A funerary monument dedicated to Cassia Severa by her husband and mother-in-law, with a mention of a freedman.

EDCS-05400927.translation: Sextus Petronius Successor, son of Marcus, an Augustalis and member of the VIvirate, ordered this to be made by his will for himself and for his wife Soccia Modesta, daughter of Marcus, and for his father Marcus Petronius Marcellus, son of Marcus, and for his brother Marcus Petronius Marcello, son of Marcus, and for his mother Grania Prima, and for his sister Petronia Exsorata, daughter of Marcus, and for his sister Petronia Vitali, daughter of Marcus. Lucius Caleius Modestus, son of Titus, supervised the construction.
EDCS-05400927.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Sextus Petronius Successor, listing numerous family members, with construction supervised by Lucius Caleius Modestus.

EDCS-05400928.translation: Gaius Gaiellus, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, a boatman.
EDCS-05400928.summary: A tombstone for Gaius Gaiellus, identifying his tribe and occupation as a boatman.

EDCS-05400929.translation: To the departed spirits. For Acutia Sabina, daughter of Quintus, a most virtuous woman. Quintus Vequasius Fortunatus made this for himself while alive, at his own expense.
EDCS-05400929.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Quintus Vequasius Fortunatus to his wife Acutia Sabina, made during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400930.translation: Titus Valerius Clemens, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, for himself and for his father Titus Valerius Sulla, son of Titus, and for his mother Veratia Maxuma, daughter of Gaius, and for his son Titus Valerius Maro, son of Titus, and for his son Titus Valerius Magnus, son of Titus, and for his wife Annia Supera, daughter of Publius, and for [his daughter]... daughter of Titus.
EDCS-05400930.summary: A funerary monument commissioned by Titus Valerius Clemens for himself and his deceased family members including parents, sons, wife, and a daughter.

EDCS-05400931.translation: Set up by the living. Quintus Veiquasius Optatus, freedman of Quintus, a worshipper of sacred rites.
EDCS-05400931.summary: An epitaph for Quintus Veiquasius Optatus, a freedman, who set up the monument himself during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400932.translation: To the departed spirits. Quintus Vettius Pansa, son of Quintus, a member of the IIIIvirate.
EDCS-05400932.summary: A fragment of a funerary monument for Quintus Vettius Pansa, identifying his father and his position as a magistrate.

EDCS-05400935.translation: Made by the living. Marcus Blaesius Quintus made this for himself and for his wife Magia Severa.
EDCS-05400935.summary: A monument made by Marcus Blaesius Quintus for himself and his wife Magia Severa during their lifetimes.

EDCS-05400936.translation: [Freedman]ianius, freedman of Publius. Ommius. [Freedman]ianius, freedman of Titus. Rebellius.
EDCS-05400936.summary: A fragmented inscription possibly recording the names and freedman status of several individuals.

EDCS-05400938.translation: [To the] August Lares. [---]ius Marcellus, son of Marcus. [---]us, son of Gaius Causo.
EDCS-05400938.summary: A fragmented inscription likely a dedication to the Lares, naming two individuals.

EDCS-05400939.translation: To the Matrons. Gaius Vennonius Macer willingly, joyfully, and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05400939.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Matrons by Gaius Vennonius Macer.

EDCS-05400941.translation: Coccia, freedwoman of Lucius Erotis, for herself and for her husband Lucius Coccius Strato, freedman of Lucius...
EDCS-05400941.summary: This is a funerary inscription commemorating Coccia and her husband, Lucius Coccius Strato, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400942.translation: Lucius Ennius Lucintus, son of Publius (of the Camilia tribe), and his wife Mettia Velta, daughter of Quintus, set this up.
EDCS-05400942.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Lucius Ennius Lucintus and his wife Mettia Velta, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400943.translation: [Firmus], son of Gaius, of the Albius [family]?
EDCS-05400943.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription identifying a man named Firmus, son of Gaius, possibly from the Albius family, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-05400944.translation: To Victoria. Vicinia Campani willingly and joyfully paid her vow.
EDCS-05400944.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Victoria by Vicinia Campani.

EDCS-05400946.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Titus Liburnius Valens arranged for the erection of this monument for Baburia Afrodiate at his own expense.
EDCS-05400946.summary: This is a funerary inscription commissioned by Titus Liburnius Valens for Baburia Afrodiate, dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400947.translation: Lucius Colianius Rufus, son of Gaius, and his wife Caesia Quinta, daughter of Quintus; Marcus Colianius Celer, son of Lucius; Gaius Colianius, son of Lucius; Lucius Colianius, son of Lucius; and Coliania Rufa, daughter of Lucius. Frontage 31 feet, depth 41 feet.
EDCS-05400947.summary: This is a funerary inscription for members of the Colianius family, indicating their burial plot size, likely dating to the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05400948.translation: Gaius Iulius Euphrosynus [erected this] for [his] merits.
EDCS-05400948.summary: This inscription, potentially funerary or dedicatory, refers to Gaius Iulius Euphrosynus and his merits, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-05400949.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription identifying Vilagenia, daughter of Vettius, with an uncertain date.

EDCS-05400951.translation: Sacred to the Matrons. Varius Tenax willingly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05400951.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the Matrons by Varius Tenax.

EDCS-05400952.translation: Sacred to Silvanus. Varius Tenax gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05400952.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the god Silvanus by Varius Tenax, likely a private individual fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-05400953.summary: This is a funerary epitaph naming Cesonia Momma, daughter of Marcus, indicating her family lineage.

EDCS-05400954.translation: Gaius Cobianius Maximus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05400954.summary: This is an epitaph naming Gaius Cobianius Maximus, son of Gaius, likely a Roman citizen identifying his lineage.

EDCS-05400955.translation: Of Sextus Lucanus, son of Publius.
EDCS-05400955.summary: This is an inscription likely part of a tomb or monument, identifying Sextus Lucanus, son of Publius.

EDCS-05400956.translation: To Gaius Lucanus Cenonus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-05400956.summary: This is an inscription, possibly funerary or dedicatory, honoring Gaius Lucanus Cenonus, son of Lucius.

EDCS-05400957.translation: Of Quintus Moavius, son of Ivius Quintus.
EDCS-05400957.summary: This inscription names Quintus Moavius, son of Ivius Quintus, likely part of a tomb or monument.

EDCS-05400958.translation: Lucius Moesianus Lucullus, son of Lucius.
EDCS-05400958.summary: This is an epitaph naming Lucius Moesianus Lucullus, son of Lucius, likely a Roman citizen.

EDCS-05400959.translation: Of Gaius Valerius Adictiacus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05400959.summary: This inscription likely forms part of a tomb or monument, identifying Gaius Valerius Adictiacus, son of Gaius.

EDCS-05400960.translation: Max... Viasonia, daughter of Titus, wife of [---].
EDCS-05400960.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph naming Viasonia, daughter of Titus, and identifying her as a wife.

EDCS-05400961.summary: This is an inscription, likely funerary or dedicatory, honoring Marcello Venialio, identified as a son.

EDCS-05400962.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of an individual, likely on a tombstone or a similar marker.

EDCS-05400965.translation: To the Spirits of the Underworld. Catavignus, son of Ivomagus, a soldier of the 3rd Cohort of Britons, under the century of Gesatus. He lived 25 years and served 6 years. Paternus of the army of Raetia, his heir, had this made for his dearest fellow soldier.
EDCS-05400965.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a soldier who served in the 3rd Cohort of Britons, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-05400966.translation: Gaius Arius Volianius and his son Gaius.
EDCS-05400966.summary: This inscription likely records the names of two individuals, perhaps father and son, possibly on a monument or tomb.

EDCS-05400967.translation: Baebia Vetla, daughter of Sextus, of the tribe Camilia, ordered this to be made in her will for Publius Baebius Parmensis, son of Lucius, of the tribe Camilia, her dearest husband; Lucius, her son, and Polla, daughter of Polla Lebronia, wife of Tertius, Polla the daughter, the heirs, had this made.
EDCS-05400967.summary: This funerary inscription records the commission of a tomb by Baebia Vetla for her husband, Publius Baebius Parmensis, and her children and the wife of her son acted as heirs.

EDCS-05400968.summary: This inscription simply provides the name and filiation of an individual, likely a tomb marker.

EDCS-05400969.translation: Sacred to Victoria. Gaius Viccius Narcissus willingly, gladly, and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05400969.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to the goddess Victoria by Gaius Viccius Narcissus.

EDCS-05400970.translation: Cominius Maxsumus, son of Marcus, of the tribe Camilia, a VIvir Augustalis, made [this] while alive.
EDCS-05400970.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument made by a local magistrate (VIvir Augustalis) during his lifetime.

EDCS-05400971.translation: Gaius Petronius Plundianius, son of Publius, of the tribe Camilia, for himself and for Mettia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, his wife, and for Gaius Petronius Maximus, his son, and for Gaius Petronius Severus, his son, and for Publius Petronius Firmus, his son, and for Titus Petronius Sextus, his son.
EDCS-05400971.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicating a tomb for Gaius Petronius Plundianius, his wife, and their four sons.

EDCS-05400972.translation: Publius Valerius Severus, son of Publius, of the tribe Camilia.
EDCS-05400972.summary: This inscription records the name and filiation of an individual, likely on a tombstone or a similar marker.

EDCS-05400973.translation: To Aulus Aurelius Blaienius, son of Aulus, of the tribe Camilia(?). Gaius Aurelius Secundus, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05400973.summary: This inscription appears to record two individuals, possibly relatives, with their names and filiations, likely on a tomb or a dedicatory monument.

EDCS-05400974.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for a woman named Cassia Secunda, identified by her father's name.

EDCS-05400975.translation: Cornelia Supera, daughter of Lucius, ordered this to be made by her will. Lucius Veustanius Niger, son of Lucius, saw to its construction.
EDCS-05400975.summary: This is a funerary epitaph commissioned by Cornelia Supera and constructed by Lucius Veustanius Niger, likely her relative or heir.

EDCS-05400976.translation: Firmius Lucanus Gemini, son of Firmius.
EDCS-05400976.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Firmius Lucanus Gemini, son of Firmius.

EDCS-05400977.translation: and for his daughter Velliae. Velagostius Modestus.
EDCS-05400977.summary: This fragmented epitaph names Velagostius Modestus and mentions his daughter Velliae.

EDCS-05400978.translation: Valeria Prisca, daughter of Titus, lived and placed this, and for Valerius Publius Secundus Alion, soldier of the Fourth Legion, son of Gaius, and for Gaius Valerius Fronton, son of Gaius.
EDCS-05400978.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Valeria Prisca, daughter of Titus, for her husband Valerius Publius Secundus Alion, a soldier in the Fourth Legion, and for her son Gaius Valerius Fronton.

EDCS-05400979.translation: Titus Ennius Secundus, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe, [placed this] for Coellia Tertulla, daughter of Gaius, his wife. Titus Ennius [---] of the Camilia tribe, [---] divine...
EDCS-05400979.summary: This funerary epitaph records Titus Ennius Secundus honoring his wife Coellia Tertulla and possibly other family members, perhaps dating to the 1st or 2nd century AD.

EDCS-05400980.translation: Sex Major, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe.
EDCS-05400980.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Sex Major, son of Marcus, belonging to the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-05400981.summary: This is a fragmented inscription, possibly a funerary marker, identifying P. Ricci Celeris.

EDCS-05400982.translation: Lucius Veltius Bassus, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, placed this while alive for himself and for Aurelia Tertia, daughter of Titus, his wife, [---].
EDCS-05400982.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Lucius Veltius Bassus for himself and his wife Aurelia Tertia.

EDCS-05400985.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Manilius Eutyches. Manilia Lupa [erected this] for her husband and son, and Manilius Lupus and Ursus [erected this] for their father and brother, who deserved well.
EDCS-05400985.summary: This funerary inscription is dedicated by Manilia Lupa to her husband and son, and by Manilius Lupus and Ursus to their father and brother.

EDCS-05400986.translation: Veccalia, daughter of Lucius, Polla; Cominia, daughter of Titus, Secunda, daughter.
EDCS-05400986.summary: This is a funerary inscription naming Veccalia and Cominia, identifying their fathers and patronymics, likely marking their graves.

EDCS-05400988.translation: To Gaius Sextius Spectatus, standard-bearer of the I Praetoria Pia Vindex cohort, Gaius Titius Marcellinus, beneficiarius of the tribune of the same cohort, (erected this) for his well-deserving (status).
EDCS-05400988.summary: This is a dedication to a standard-bearer of a Praetorian cohort, erected by a beneficiarius, likely from the 2nd century AD.

EDCS-05400989.translation: Sacred to the Divine Shades. Taietia Euterpe made this for her well-deserving life companion and for Lucius Taietius Apollinaris, their son, and for themselves and their descendants.
EDCS-05400989.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a woman for her partner and son, and for herself and her descendants, invoking the Divine Shades, likely from the 1st-3rd century AD.

EDCS-05400990.translation: Here rests in good memory John, who lived for more or less 34 years and passed away on the 4th day before the Kalends of October, under the consulship of Faustus the Younger, vir clarissimus.
EDCS-05400990.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of Johannes, providing his age at death and the consular date (Faustus the Younger), indicating a late Roman period.

EDCS-05400991.translation: To the Divine Shades. Gnaeus Lucretius Lucretianus (dedicated this) for his well-deserving fosterlings Agathemerus and Eutyches.
EDCS-05400991.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Gnaeus Lucretius Lucretianus for his fosterlings Agathemerus and Eutyches, invoking the Divine Shades.

EDCS-05400992.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Hateria Privata, daughter of Quintus.
EDCS-05400992.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Hateria Privata, daughter of Quintus, invoking the Divine Shades.

EDCS-05400993.translation: To the Divine Shades. Aulus Servilius Philodoxus made this for his most beloved wife Servilia Restituta, and for himself.
EDCS-05400993.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Aulus Servilius Philodoxus for his wife Servilia Restituta, and also for himself, invoking the Divine Shades.

EDCS-05400994.translation: Urbicius, a slave of Honesteiocatus, aged 17 years.
EDCS-05400994.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Urbicius, a young slave, stating his age and owner.

EDCS-05400999.translation: To the Divine Shades. Fortunius, Alexander, and Hermes, freedmen, purchased this sarcophagus for their most worthy patron, Aurelius Hilarus, freedman of Augustus, overseer of the child footmen.
EDCS-05400999.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Aurelius Hilarus, a freedman of Augustus and overseer, for whom his freedmen purchased a sarcophagus.

EDCS-05401000.translation: To Aurelia Laudice, his excellent wife, well-deserving. Lupercus, dispensator of the private office, (dedicated this).
EDCS-05401000.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lupercus, a dispensator, to his wife Aurelia Laudice.

EDCS-05401001.translation: Publius Aelius Pylades, freedman of the emperor, established the theatre; Lucius Aurelius Pylades, freedman of the emperors, his student, completed it.
EDCS-05401001.summary: This inscription records the construction of a theatre, established by Publius Aelius Pylades and completed by his student Lucius Aurelius Pylades, likely during the period of joint emperors.

EDCS-05401002.translation: To the memory of Lucius Altilius Epictetus Callistinus, who lived 4 years, 3 months, and 28 days. Lucius Altilius Epictetus and Flavia Calliste, parents, for their dearest son.
EDCS-05401002.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young child, Lucius Altilius Epictetus Callistinus, set up by his parents, Lucius Altilius Epictetus and Flavia Calliste.

EDCS-05401003.translation: Cornelia Secunda, wife, made this for Marcus Antonius Hilarius, son of Balbus, and for her son Lucius Herennius Nigellio, son of Lucius, and for Publius Caninius Felix.
EDCS-05401003.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument erected by Cornelia Secunda for her husband Marcus Antonius Hilarius and her son Lucius Herennius Nigellio, and also for Publius Caninius Felix.

EDCS-05401004.translation: Lucius Apusulenus Pollio is buried here.
EDCS-05401004.summary: This is a simple burial inscription for Lucius Apusulenus Pollio.

EDCS-05401005.translation: Genialis, the husband, for his incomparable wife Clodia Helpidi.
EDCS-05401005.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by a husband, Genialis, for his wife, Clodia Helpidi.

EDCS-05401006.translation: To the departed spirits of Lucius Cominius Hermes, freedman of Lucius. To the departed spirits of Cominia Hora, freedwoman of Lucius. Cominia Zele, daughter, made [this] for the well-deserving.
EDCS-05401006.summary: This inscription records funerary dedications to Lucius Cominius Hermes and Cominia Hora, made by Cominia Zele for them and possibly herself.

EDCS-05401007.translation: To the departed spirits. Gaius Cominius Valerianus made [this] for his most dutiful son, Gaius Cominius Thallus, deserving.
EDCS-05401007.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Gaius Cominius Valerianus for his son Gaius Cominius Thallus.

EDCS-05401008.translation: To the departed spirits of Dionysius, freedman of the emperors, who lived 24 years and 6 months. Nebridius.
EDCS-05401008.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Dionysius, freedman of the emperors, who lived 24 years and 6 months, set up by Nebridius.

EDCS-05401009.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Iulius Messor made this for his most dutiful brother, Marcus Iulius Adeptus.
EDCS-05401009.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by Marcus Iulius Messor for his brother Marcus Iulius Adeptus.

EDCS-05401010.translation: Arnius for his mistress Iulia Urbica.
EDCS-05401010.summary: This inscription records Arnius dedicating something to his mistress, Iulia Urbica.

EDCS-05401011.translation: To Junia Platonis, my dearest wife, Flavius Justus, her husband, [erected this].
EDCS-05401011.summary: A husband dedicates a tomb to his wife, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401012.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Negelia Noni, daughter of Titus, a most rare woman and wife, who lived 42 years. Marcus Ulpius Theophilus [erected this] to his dearest and most chaste wife, with whom he lived for 24 years, 6 months, and 11 days, without a single complaint.
EDCS-05401012.summary: A husband dedicates a tomb to his wife, providing her age at death and the duration of their marriage, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401013.translation: Octavia Philumina, a freedwoman, is buried here.
EDCS-05401013.summary: A tombstone marks the burial place of Octavia Philumina, a freedwoman, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401015.translation: Aulus Sergius Epaphroditus and Aulus Sergius Sergianus, his son, made [this] for Sergia Trophime, [their] wife and mother.
EDCS-05401015.summary: A husband and son dedicate a tomb to Sergia Trophime, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401016.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Pedanius Ursus made [this] for his incomparable friend, well-deserving, Caius Trocinus Honesimus.
EDCS-05401016.summary: Lucius Pedanius Ursus dedicates a tomb to his friend, Caius Trocinus Honesimus, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401018.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Gaius Urbinus Victor.
EDCS-05401018.summary: A tomb dedication to Gaius Urbinus Victor, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401019.summary: A simple epitaph for Chrysaeus, indicating peace in death, likely from the Late Roman or Early Christian period.

EDCS-05401020.translation: Magnus, a soldier of the happy numbering of the Illyrian legions, rests here in good peace. He lived in this world approximately 35 years. He was buried on the 7th day before the Ides of August, in the reign of our lord emperor Maurice Tiberius, Father of the Fatherland, Augustus, in the eighth year of his reign and the eighth indiction.
EDCS-05401020.summary: A soldier's burial record dating to the reign of Emperor Maurice Tiberius (late 6th century AD).

EDCS-05401021.translation: Here rests with good memory Sanctulus, subdeacon, in peace. He lived approximately 80 years. His deposit was on the 6th day before the Kalends of May, in the consulship of the most distinguished man Albinus, consul.
EDCS-05401021.summary: A burial record for Sanctulus, a subdeacon, with a date related to the consulship of Albinus, likely in the Late Roman period.

EDCS-05401022.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Lucius Faenius Zosimus made [this] for himself and for Faenia Heurete, [his daughter], and for his descendants and their posterity.
EDCS-05401022.summary: Lucius Faenius Zosimus dedicates a tomb for himself, his daughter, and descendants, likely in the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401023.translation: Gaius Gellius, son of Gaius, chief priest, lived for 51 years. Died on the fourth day before the Ides of December.
EDCS-05401023.summary: A funerary epigram for Gaius Gellius, a chief priest, who died at the age of 51.

EDCS-05401026.translation: Monument of Publius Vatinius Secundus, son of Titus [---]. His wife Quarta, daughter of Lucius [---], [erected this monument].
EDCS-05401026.summary: A funerary monument for Publius Vatinius Secundus and his wife Quarta, with some text missing.

EDCS-05401027.summary: A fragmentary inscription mentioning a person named Crescentianus, with much of the text lost.

EDCS-05401028.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus iae Cai filiae Summae matri Iuniae Quinti filiae Secundae sorori vivus Quintus Iunius Quinti filius Optatus\n
EDCS-05401028.translation: To the Divine Spirits. Quintus Iunius Optatus, son of Quintus, dedicated this to his mother Iunia Secunda, daughter of Quintus, and to his sister Summa, daughter of Caius, while he was alive.
EDCS-05401028.summary: A dedication by Quintus Iunius Optatus to his mother and sister, likely a family tomb inscription.

EDCS-05401029.translation: Lucius Nemanius Severus, of the Camilia tribe, and his mother Papiria Prisca, freedwoman of Sextus, erected this for Valeria Procla, daughter of Decimus, for themselves and their family, while alive.
EDCS-05401029.summary: A funerary monument erected by Lucius Nemanius Severus and his mother Papiria Prisca for Valeria Procla, indicating it was a self-funded monument for the living.

EDCS-05401032.translation: To Publius Metilius Tertullinus Vennonianus, of the Falerna tribe, son of Publius, a most distinguished man, quaestor designate of Laurentum Lavinium, patron, by the urban plebs of Albingaunum. The site was granted by decree of the decurions.
EDCS-05401032.summary: An honorific inscription from the urban plebs of Albingaunum to Publius Metilius Tertullinus Vennonianus, a patron and high-ranking official, with the site granted by decree.

EDCS-05401033.text_edition: \n Marcus Valerius Bradua Mauricus clarissimae memoriae vir consul pontifex sodalis Hadrianalis curator operum publicorum curator aquarum sacrae urbis et Miniciae censitor provinciae Aquetanicae sic proconsul provinciae Africae balneum quod vivos inchoaverat Quintus Virius Egnatius Sulpicius Priscus consularis pontifex et flamen divi Severi curator aquarum sacrae urbis et Miniciae eodemque tempore praefectus alimentorum perfectum Albingaunensibus adsignavit\n
EDCS-05401033.translation: Marcus Valerius Bradua Mauricus, of most distinguished memory, consul, priest, member of the Hadrianales, curator of public works, curator of the sacred water supply of the city and the Minicia, census-taker of the province of Aquitaine, and former proconsul of the province of Africa, dedicated the baths which he had begun during his lifetime to the people of Albingaunum. Quintus Virius Egnatius Sulpicius Priscus, ex-consul, priest, and flamen of the deified Severus, curator of the sacred water supply of the city and the Minicia, and at the same time prefect of the alimentary program, completed and assigned them to the people of Albingaunum.
EDCS-05401033.summary: A complex inscription detailing the dedication of public baths by Marcus Valerius Bradua Mauricus and their completion and assignment by Quintus Virius Egnatius Sulpicius Priscus, highlighting their significant public careers and civic benefactions.

EDCS-05401034.translation: To Publius Mucilius Verus, son of Publius, of the Publilia tribe, Roman knight, with public horse, patron of the municipality, tribune of the III Gallica legion, census-taker of the province of Thracia, an excellent citizen, always concerned for the safety of the municipalities, by the urban plebs.
EDCS-05401034.summary: An honorific inscription from the urban plebs to Publius Mucilius Verus, a Roman knight and prominent civic figure who served in the military and administration.

EDCS-05401035.translation: Lucius Aurelius Meleager, son of Lucius, aedile [---], twice prefect, quaestor [erected this] for himself and for Aurelia Polla, daughter of Lucius [---], and for his brother Publius Aurelius [---], son of Lucius [---].
EDCS-05401035.summary: A funerary inscription for Lucius Aurelius Meleager, his sister Aurelia Polla, and his brother Publius Aurelius, listing their official positions and familial relationships.

EDCS-05401036.translation: For Cassius Valerianus, an innocent man of principal rank in the city, who lived for about 70 years, of good memory. His wife and sons erected this. Interred on the 5th day before the Kalends of January.
EDCS-05401036.summary: A funerary inscription for Cassius Valerianus, honoring his character and longevity, erected by his family and noting his burial date.

EDCS-05401037.translation: Publius Granius Hyla, freedman of Publius, the Augustalis, made this while alive for himself and for his freedwoman mother, Quartilla.
EDCS-05401037.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Granius Hyla and his mother Quartilla, who made the monument during their lifetime.

EDCS-05401038.inscription_type: tituli operum, tituli sacri, tituli sepulcrales

EDCS-05401039.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Marcus Valerius Rectus.

EDCS-05401040.translation: To the living, he made this for himself and for Pollia Amabilis, freedwoman of Pollia. To Marcus Valerius Salvius Libra, son of Titus, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-05401040.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius Salvius Libra and his freedwoman Pollia Amabilis, made by the dedicatee during his lifetime.

EDCS-05401041.translation: Cornelia Procula, daughter of Quintus, mother of Marcus Vibullius Proculus, son of Publius, erected this for her son, who lived 17 years, an excellent son.
EDCS-05401041.summary: A funerary epitaph erected by a mother for her son, Marcus Vibullius Proculus.

EDCS-05401042.translation: Here rests Heliades, of good memory. We ask you, Christ, that you deign to help her. Call her forth with your calling; snatch her from the hands of the devil, who praised you during the days of her life, so that she may rejoice in the future life with your mercy. Free her, Christ, and deign to receive her and lead her into your place of blessedness. Let your piety precede, because she remained in your love during her youth. Therefore, Lord, grant her in the future life what she asked of you in the present, and do not repay her for her deeds, but you, Lord, who are merciful, deign to...
EDCS-05401042.summary: A Christian funerary inscription requesting Christ to aid the deceased Heliades, ensuring her salvation and eternal rest.

EDCS-05401043.translation: Here rests in peace Honorata, of good memory, a most distinguished and pious woman, wife of Tzittanus, count and tribune, who lived in this world for 40 years. She was buried on the day before the Kalends of February, in the first indiction, in the third year of our lord Justinus, perpetual Augustus. I beg you by almighty God and Jesus Christ of Nazareth, do not touch me nor violate my tomb, for you will plead your case with me before the tribunal of the eternal judge.
EDCS-05401043.summary: A Christian funerary inscription for Honorata, wife of a count and tribune, buried in the 6th century, warning against tomb violation.

EDCS-05401044.translation: I, Mari[---]vv, place these limbs of yours, O Christ, into our souls. How much do I dedicate to you? Marinace S VVRARP[---]novavi.
EDCS-05401044.summary: A fragmented inscription dedicating something to Christ, possibly a personal offering or tomb.

EDCS-05401046.translation: Marcus Baebius, son of Marcus, 31 years old.
EDCS-05401046.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the age of Marcus Baebius.

EDCS-05401047.translation: To Marcus Valerius Muscio, son of Publius, and to Valeria Poeni, daughter of Marcus, his wife.
EDCS-05401047.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Valerius Muscio and his wife Valeria Poeni.

EDCS-05401048.translation: Of Publius Varius Secundus, son of Publius.
EDCS-05401048.summary: A funerary epitaph for Publius Varius Secundus.

EDCS-05401049.translation: To Quintus Voconius, son of Titus.
EDCS-05401049.summary: An epitaph for Quintus Voconius, son of Titus, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401050.summary: An epitaph for Matius, freedman of Tiberius, who was also known as Tertius, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401053.translation: Titus Retius Alebo's son, a freedman, erected this for Titus Voconius, son of Marcus, of the Montanus family, and for his brother Tertius, son of Marcus. The heir was instructed by will to have it made.
EDCS-05401053.summary: A funerary monument set up by a freedman and heir for two brothers, Titus Voconius Montanus and his brother Tertius, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401054.translation: Marcus Cassius Messor, duovir with judicial authority, dedicated this altar with its base to Hercules, having made it public property.
EDCS-05401054.summary: Marcus Cassius Messor, a local magistrate, dedicated a public altar to Hercules, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401057.translation: Marcus Terentius Optatus, son of Publius, of the Publilia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-05401057.summary: An epitaph for Marcus Terentius Optatus, son of Publius, initiated by his will, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401058.translation: Lucius Licinius, son of Gaius, of the Pupinia tribe, [---], [---], [---].
EDCS-05401058.summary: A fragmentary funerary inscription for Lucius Licinius, son of Gaius, of the Pupinia tribe, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401059.translation: To Victoria Aeterna, of the unconquered Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Autolycus, restorer of the fortress, Marcus Valerius Caminas, dedicated this.
EDCS-05401059.summary: A dedication to Victoria Aeterna and Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Valerius Caminas, who is also identified as Autolycus, a restorer of a fortress, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401060.translation: Marcus C. Anthius fulfilled his vow to Apollo.
EDCS-05401060.summary: A votive inscription recording Marcus C. Anthius fulfilling a vow to Apollo, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401061.translation: Sacred to Juno Regina, for the honor and memory of Verginia Paternas, daughter of Publius. Publius Verginius Rhodion, his freedman, in his own name and in the name of his wife Metilia Tertullina, priestess, and of their children Verginia Quieta, Paternas, Restituta, and Quieta, placed this with his own money.
EDCS-05401061.summary: A dedication to Juno Regina by Publius Verginius Rhodion, a freedman, honoring his wife Metilia Tertullina and their children, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401063.translation: Ordered by will to be made: to Manius Atilius Alpinus, son of Lucius, of the Falerna tribe, aedile; to Atilia Veamona, daughter of Manius; to Lucius Atilius Cupito, son of Manius; to Gaius Atilius Alpinus, son of Manius; to Manius Atilius Priscus, son of Manius; to Atilia Posilla, daughter of Manius; to Atilia Secunda, daughter of Manius; and to Licinia Cupita, daughter of Gaius, granddaughter.
EDCS-05401063.summary: A funerary monument listing multiple family members, initiated by will, for Manius Atilius Alpinus and other relatives, dating from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401064.translation: Quintus Mantius Placidus, son of Quintus, of the Palatina tribe, a public horseman, aedile, and twice a priest of Lanuvium, was set up by Lucius Polfenius Cerdo and Mantia Lucida with their children Mantis Lucife and Zenio, at their own expense.
EDCS-05401064.summary: This is a funerary or honorific inscription dedicated to Quintus Mantius Placidus by his family, likely from the Roman period.

EDCS-05401065.translation: Aulus T. son of Quintus P. dedicated [it?].
EDCS-05401065.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication, likely from a private monument, identifying the dedicator.

EDCS-05401066.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription likely honoring a person named Pompeius Macro.

EDCS-05401081.translation: To the August Victoria, Vibius Caestius [dedicated?].
EDCS-05401081.summary: This is a fragmentary dedication to the goddess Victoria Augusta.

EDCS-05401082.translation: Marcus Exomnius Severus, son of Maximus, of the Pollia tribe, twice duumvir, made this while alive for himself and for Disiania Blaius, daughter of Maximus, his wife.
EDCS-05401082.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Marcus Exomnius Severus, a local magistrate, for himself and his wife.

EDCS-05401083.translation: To Victoria Augusta, Metilius Secundus, attendant of the Emperor, fulfilled his vow willingly and gladly for his merits.
EDCS-05401083.summary: This is a votive inscription to Victoria Augusta by Metilius Secundus, an imperial attendant.

EDCS-05401084.translation: Lucius Domitius Secundus, son of Spurius, of the Sabatina tribe, [set this up] for himself and for Coifilasias Supera, his wife, for his mother Domitia Tertia, daughter of Quintus, and for Vibius Salvius, the magistrate.
EDCS-05401084.summary: This is a family funerary inscription set up by Lucius Domitius Secundus.

EDCS-05401085.translation: While alive, they made [this] for the departed spirits: Marcus Didi Sabinianus, aedile and duumvir, and his wife Mattoria Marciana, and their sons Didi Marc[---] Marcellus Ian[---]anus, and Moccius Iustus, the son-in-law, placed [this] for their parents.
EDCS-05401085.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by the family of Marcus Didi Sabinianus, a local magistrate.

EDCS-05401086.translation: [---] for the curator of the public affairs of Pedona [---], curator of the public affairs of Cabur[---], curator of the public affairs of Germa[---], for Valeria Nepotilla, his most devoted wife, who lived 39 years, 3 months, and 27 days [---].
EDCS-05401086.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription for Valeria Nepotilla, wife of a man who held multiple curatorial positions.

EDCS-05401087.translation: Rinnio Novicio, son of Mulio. While alive, Rinnins Karius, his son, made [this] for his father and his brother.
EDCS-05401087.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by Rinnins Karius for his father and brother.

EDCS-05401088.translation: Enistalus, Ponelius the father, his wife Enania, his son Ulatunus, the son Premelius, his wife Velisa, the son Veturus - while alive; be well, and you.
EDCS-05401088.summary: This funerary monument records the living members of the Enistali family, likely belonging to a local elite and dating from the early Imperial period.

EDCS-05401089.translation: Diogenes dedicated this to Julia Tyrannis, freedwoman of Marcus, and to her son Gaius Julius Aphrodatus.
EDCS-05401089.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Diogenes for Julia Tyrannis, a freedwoman, and her son, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-05401090.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph naming Quintus Nigidius, son of Spurius, possibly from the Roman Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-05401091.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Plenus [---] to his wife Attia [---].
EDCS-05401091.summary: This is a fragment of a funerary dedication to the departed spirits, mentioning Plenus and his wife Attia, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401092.summary: This is a very brief inscription, possibly funerary or dedicatory, mentioning Vicino Comiacus and an unclear phrase, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401095.summary: This is a funerary epitaph, possibly recording an ancestor or relative, naming Velaco son of Blaisicius Enicus, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401099.translation: Sacred to the Matrones. Lucius Publilius Rapax paid his vow willingly and with joy.
EDCS-05401099.summary: This is a votive dedication to the Matrones, a group of female deities, by Lucius Publilius Rapax, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401102.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To his most beloved wife and deserving of good from him, Victorina, Flaminalis, slave of Marcus Tarquinius Memoris, the tax collector of the Quadragesima (customs duty) of Gaul, the steward of the Pedonensis station.
EDCS-05401102.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a steward and tax collector in Roman Gaul to his beloved wife Victorina, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-05401103.translation: To Nevius Mearius, his dearest friend, and to Velacostai Velaiuniai, his wife.
EDCS-05401103.summary: This is a funerary dedication from a friend to Nevius Mearius and his wife Velacostai Velaiuniai, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401104.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription recording the erection of a monument by Vesuav and others, possibly funerary or dedicatory, from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401105.translation: To the departed spirits. Marcus Alpinius Ingenus and Attia Verina, daughter, made this monument while alive for their very dear Vettia Faustina, mother.
EDCS-05401105.summary: This funerary epitaph was erected by a son-in-law and daughter for Vettia Faustina.

EDCS-05401106.translation: Vibius Veamonius Gallus, son of Iemmius, his wife Mocca Ennania, and his sons erected this monument deservedly.
EDCS-05401106.summary: This epitaph records the erection of a monument by Vibius Veamonius Gallus, his wife, and sons.

EDCS-05401107.translation: [---] Urbicius(?) son of Div[---] son of Peloxius[---]FT[---]
EDCS-05401107.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph or dedication, with names and filiations mostly lost.

EDCS-05401110.translation: To Jupiter Best and Greatest. The brothers Optatus and Sabinus gladly and deservedly paid their vow, along with all their family.
EDCS-05401110.summary: This dedication to Jupiter was made by two brothers, Optatus and Sabinus, who fulfilled a vow.

EDCS-05401111.translation: Sacred to Victoria. Ulattius Adiutor, veteran of the Emperor, ordered this temple to be built by his will; [---]tius and [---]nius built [---].
EDCS-05401111.summary: This inscription records the construction of a temple dedicated to Victoria, ordered by a veteran named Ulattius Adiutor.

EDCS-05401112.summary: This very brief inscription records the dedication of wagons.

EDCS-05401113.translation: To the god Leucimalacus Mars. Marcus Fuscius Secundus, decurion of the Quirina tribe, gladly and deservedly paid his vow.
EDCS-05401113.summary: This dedication to the god Mars Leucimalacus was made by Marcus Fuscius Secundus, a decurion.

EDCS-05401114.translation: Atilia Polla, daughter of Caius, made this while alive for herself and for her husband Tatius Supeirus, son of Teitus.
EDCS-05401114.summary: This funerary monument was erected by Atilia Polla for herself and her husband Tatius Supeirus.

EDCS-05401336.translation: To the Emperor Caesar Flavius Valerius Constantinus, the Pious, Fortunate, Unconquered Augustus.
EDCS-05401336.summary: This is an imperial dedication to Emperor Constantine I.

EDCS-05401337.translation: Antoninus Pius Augustus ordered this to be placed.
EDCS-05401337.summary: This inscription records an order by Emperor Antoninus Pius to place something.

EDCS-05401338.summary: This inscription records the name of Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus, likely part of a larger dedication or monument.

EDCS-05401341.translation: Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered [this] to be set up. 599.
EDCS-05401341.summary: This inscription records that Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered a monument to be set up, indicated by a numerical value possibly related to its cost or location.

EDCS-05401343.translation: Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered [this] to be set up. 560.
EDCS-05401343.summary: This inscription records that Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered a monument to be set up, indicated by a numerical value possibly related to its cost or location.

EDCS-05401344.translation: Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered [this] to be set up. 10.
EDCS-05401344.summary: This inscription records that Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered a monument to be set up, indicated by the number 10, possibly representing units or cost.

EDCS-05401345.translation: Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered [this] to be set up.
EDCS-05401345.summary: This inscription records that Emperor Antoninus Pius Felix Augustus ordered a monument to be set up.

EDCS-05401346.summary: This inscription begins with the name of Emperor Antoninus, likely part of a larger inscription.

EDCS-05401728.summary: This inscription names Optatus as a pontifex and Secundus as an augur, indicating their religious offices, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401741.translation: Lucius Aelius Severus, son of Aelius Philherotis
EDCS-05401741.summary: This inscription is a gentilician name, identifying Lucius Aelius Severus as the son of Aelius Philherotis, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401742.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Veltius and Pullania Secundina, siblings, [dedicate this] to their parents.
EDCS-05401742.summary: This funerary inscription records Veltius and Pullania Secundina dedicating a monument to their parents, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401745.translation: To the spirits of the underworld: Lucius Verinus, son of Verinus.
EDCS-05401745.summary: This funerary inscription records Lucius Verinus, son of Verinus, dedicating a monument to the spirits of the underworld, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-05401746.translation: Ienesia, who was taken from the world to live eternally, not handed over to the torments of Tartarus but adorned with everlasting gifts, who lived a short time in this world so that she might depart holier to the Lord, pleasing to all in the world, more pleasing to Christ eternally, to whom she is a consecrated offering. She lived for two years, [---] months, two days. She was laid to rest on the sixth day before the Ides of June. Dinamio and Sefidus, most distinguished sirs, consuls.
EDCS-05401746.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Ienesia, dating to the consulship of Dinamio and Sefidus, likely in the 4th or 5th century CE, given the Christian references.

EDCS-05401748.translation: To Lucius Cassius, son of Spurius, father; to Geminia Quinte, daughter of Lucius, mother; to Marcus Cassius, son of Lucius, brother; to Quintus Cassius, son of Lucius, brother. Lucius Cassius, son of Caius, son; to Caesiae Secundae, daughter of Caius, daughter (his); to Muciae Rufae, wife of Marcus, wife. Caius Cassius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, ordered this to be made by his will.
EDCS-05401748.summary: This is a funerary monument inscribed by Caius Cassius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, by his will, honoring his father, mother, brothers, daughter, and wife.

EDCS-05401749.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius, to Farontius.
EDCS-05401749.summary: This is a dedication of a monument from Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius, to someone named Farontius.

EDCS-05401750.translation: Of Quintus Vibius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, Seuvonus.
EDCS-05401750.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Seuvonus, son of Quintus Vibius, of the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-06300002.translation: Of Titus Autronius, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, Tertius.
EDCS-06300002.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Tertius, son of Titus Autronius, of the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-06300003.translation: Of Domitia, daughter of Publius, the third.
EDCS-06300003.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domitia Tertia, daughter of Publius.

EDCS-06300004.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Mettia Secunda, daughter of Sextus.

EDCS-06300005.translation: To Lucius Mucius Pius, son of Lucius.
EDCS-06300005.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Mucius Pius, son of Lucius.

EDCS-06300015.translation: Quintus Veianius, son of Quintus, of the Camilia tribe, Nigro, as aedile, by his will.
EDCS-06300015.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Nigro, who held the office of aedile, inscribed by Quintus Veianius, son of Quintus, of the Camilia tribe, in accordance with his will.

EDCS-06300016.translation: Publius Cordius Quadratus, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, performed this while alive. He was one of the six priests and a decurion. For himself, and for Ennia Quinte, daughter of Publius, his wife, and for Cordia Pupa, daughter of Publius.
EDCS-06300016.summary: This is a funerary monument built by Publius Cordius Quadratus, a IIII vir and decurion, honoring himself, his wife Ennia Quinte, and their daughter Cordia Pupa.

EDCS-06300018.translation: To Vibius Aconius, son of Vibius.
EDCS-06300018.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Vibius Aconius, son of Vibius.

EDCS-06300019.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Chryseros, identified as the brother of the dedicator.

EDCS-06300023.translation: Metilius, son of Quintus, has rightly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-06300023.summary: This inscription records Metilius, son of Quintus, fulfilling a vow, likely on a religious monument.

EDCS-06300025.translation: Lucius Vettius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, from Villaco, and Publius Rufus, for their sons, erected this.
EDCS-06300025.summary: This is a dedication set up by Lucius Vettius and Publius Rufus for their sons.

EDCS-06300029.translation: Lucius Prima and Stactinus Clodius, and to Publius Clodius, freedman of Titus Publius, and to Clodia Modesta, freedwoman of Titus Publius, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-06300029.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by Lucius Prima and Stactinus Clodius for themselves and for two freedpersons, likely members of their household.

EDCS-06300030.translation: To Cassius, son of Tertius, of the Camilia tribe, Septumus, and Octavus(?), and Quartus, their mother placed (this) for her dearest sons.
EDCS-06300030.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her sons, Cassius Septumus, Octavus, and Quartus.

EDCS-06300031.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Antonia Tertia, daughter of Marcus.

EDCS-06300032.summary: This is a simple funerary dedication to Villia Suma, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-06300033.translation: To Maxsumus of the Camilia tribe, a municipal magistrate (duovir), for Calidia [---].
EDCS-06300033.summary: This inscription likely records a dedication or honorific monument for Maxsumus, a magistrate, possibly related to Calidia.

EDCS-06300038.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Cassia Cila, a freedwoman of Caius.

EDCS-06300039.translation: Gaius Caecilius [---], Gaius Caecilius [---], Publius Caecilius [---], Gaius Aurelius [---].
EDCS-06300039.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented list of names, possibly related to a family or a group, with the last name being Gaius Aurelius.

EDCS-06300045.translation: Gaius Viccius Marcellius, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, had this made under the care of his brother Quintus.
EDCS-06300045.summary: This is a funerary or dedication inscription recording that Gaius Viccius Marcellius, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, commissioned the work, overseen by his brother Quintus.

EDCS-06300046.translation: Lucius Villius Loucissus of the Camilia tribe and Gaius Villius Tertulus, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, erected (this).
EDCS-06300046.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the erection of a monument by Lucius Villius Loucissus and Gaius Villius Tertulus, both from the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-06300047.summary: This is a fragmented funerary inscription naming Sextus Flavius, son of Sextus.

EDCS-06300053.translation: Of Lucius Vettius, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe, [and] Loucisius [---].
EDCS-06300053.summary: This is a fragmented inscription naming individuals from the Vettii family, possibly related to funerary or ownership records.

EDCS-06300054.translation: Sacred to Jupiter [---]. [---]inia HIRC[---]. [---]RT Pontis. Au[gusti?] procurator, having undertaken [---].
EDCS-06300054.summary: This is a fragmented inscription likely dedicated to Jupiter, mentioning a procurator of Pontus, possibly dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-06300057.translation: [---]ri Stati. // Of Sextus Rantulanus Philogenes. // Of Lucius Caec[ilius ---].
EDCS-06300057.summary: This inscription appears to be a fragmented list of names, possibly from a funerary monument or a list of dedicants.

EDCS-06300068.translation: [---]ri Stati. // Of Sextus Rantulanus Philogenes. // Of Lucius Caec[ilius ---].
EDCS-06300068.summary: Publicia Maximilla fulfilled her vow and dedicated this gift [to a deity].

EDCS-06300070.translation: Gaius Mettius Germanus, freedman of Gaius, of the Palatina tribe, the barber.
EDCS-06300070.summary: This is an epitaph for Gaius Mettius Germanus, a barber and freedman of Gaius, belonging to the Palatina tribe.

EDCS-06300073.text_edition: \n Dianae Augustae Seia Quinti filia Sabina magistra pagi\n
EDCS-06300073.translation: To Diana Augusta, Seia Sabina, daughter of Quintus, magistrate of the district.
EDCS-06300073.summary: This inscription records a dedication to Diana Augusta by Seia Sabina, daughter of Quintus, who served as a local magistrate.

EDCS-06300074.text_edition: \n Deanae sacrum Venelia Cai filia Marcella et Valeria Luci liberta Appelia\n
EDCS-06300074.translation: Sacred to Diana. Venelia Marcella, daughter of Caius, and Appelia, freedwoman of Lucius, [dedicated this].
EDCS-06300074.summary: This is a religious dedication to the goddess Diana by two women.

EDCS-06300076.text_edition: \n Lucius Gavius Cai filius Pollia aedilis IIvir quinquennalis Gavia Luci filia Prima filia Bussenia Publi filia Nepotula uxor\n
EDCS-06300076.translation: Lucius Gavius, son of Caius, of the Pollia tribe, aedile and quinquennial duovir, and his wife Gavia Prima, daughter of Lucius, and Nepotula, daughter of Publius, wife of [---].
EDCS-06300076.summary: This inscription lists local magistrates and their family members, likely on a public monument.

EDCS-07000475.text_edition: \n Marcus Terentius Spuri filius annorum XIIX Didia Cai filia mater\n
EDCS-07000475.translation: Marcus Terentius, son of Spurius, aged 18. Didia, mother of Caius, [dedicated this].
EDCS-07000475.summary: This epitaph records the death of a young man, Marcus Terentius, and is set up by his mother.

EDCS-07000476.text_edition: \n Lucius Mercleanius filius Pollia Martialies sic miles cohortis urbanae centuria \n
EDCS-07000476.translation: Lucius Mercleanius, son of [---], of the Pollia tribe, a soldier of the urban cohort, under the centurion [---].
EDCS-07000476.summary: This inscription identifies a soldier of the urban cohort, likely on a tombstone or military dedication.

EDCS-07400315.text_edition: \n Luci Comini Cai fili Camilia Superi Iuniai sic Cai filiae Modestai sic Clarus Iunius Cai filius Secundus frater fecit de suo et vir\n
EDCS-07400315.translation: Lucius Cominius, son of Caius, of the Camilia tribe, Superus, son of Iunius, son of Caius, and his sister Modesta, and Clarus Iunius, son of Caius, the brother, made [this] from his own funds, and his husband [dedicated this].
EDCS-07400315.summary: This funerary inscription records the construction of a monument by siblings and the husband of one of them.

EDCS-07400316.text_edition: \n Petronio Marci filio Tromentina Peicio - Publius Marcus Caius filii posuerunt\n
EDCS-07400316.translation: Publius Marcus and Caius, sons of [---], of the Tromentina tribe, dedicated this to their father, Petronius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-07400316.summary: This funerary inscription records the dedication of a monument by two sons to their father.

EDCS-07400318.text_edition: \n Attiae Marci filiae Vennae Lucius Sextus Quintus Secunda fili et Caius Memmius vir posuerunt\n
EDCS-07400318.translation: Lucius Sextus Quintus and Secunda, children of Attia Vena, daughter of Marcus, and Caius Memmius, her husband, set [this] up.
EDCS-07400318.summary: This funerary inscription records the setting up of a monument by the husband and children for Attia Vena.

EDCS-07600184.text_edition: \n Caius Piranus Primus fecit Caius Piramus Philomusus fecit Petics Marsi\n
EDCS-07600184.translation: Caius Piranus Primus made [this]. Caius Piramus Philomusus made [this] for Petics, son of Marsi.
EDCS-07600184.summary: This inscription records the construction of a monument by two individuals, possibly for a third person or as a joint effort.

EDCS-08000618.translation: To the Genius of the municipality of Industrienses. Zosimus, a VIvir Augustalis, [dedicated this].
EDCS-08000618.summary: This is a religious dedication to the Genius of the town of Industrienses by a prominent local official.

EDCS-08000619.translation: Gaius Erbonius Rutundus, son of Gaius, a member of the college of six men, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow to Mercury.
EDCS-08000619.summary: This is a votive inscription by a freedman and a college official, likely from the early imperial period, dedicating a vow to Mercury.

EDCS-08000638.translation: Iulius Geminianus, with his family, willingly and deservedly fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-08000638.summary: This is a votive inscription by Iulius Geminianus and his household, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-08000639.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Peculiaris made this for her most devoted son, Manius Iunius Tranquillus, assistant of the prefect of the fabric district.
EDCS-08000639.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a mother for her son, an assistant to a prefect, probably from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08000640.translation: Passage prohibited except by permission of the owner, Publius Noni Primus.
EDCS-08000640.summary: This is a prohibitory inscription, likely marking private property and dating to the imperial period.

EDCS-08000641.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Bittia Amabilis made this for her most excellent husband, Gaius Aemilius Clemens.
EDCS-08000641.summary: This is a funerary dedication by a wife for her husband, a Roman citizen, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08000642.translation: Lucius Afranius Severus lived for 14 years. Lucius Afranius Maritimus, father, made this for his son, and Iulia Severa, mother.
EDCS-08000642.summary: This is a funerary inscription set up by the parents for their son, Lucius Afranius Severus, who died at age 14, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-08000643.translation: Gaius Alban[ius ---], son of Publius Octavius Im[---] lived 21 years [---]
EDCS-08000643.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary inscription, likely dating to the imperial period, recording the name and age of the deceased.

EDCS-08000644.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Dioscurus and Iucundilla, parents, made this for their most devoted son, aged 23 years, at their own expense.
EDCS-08000644.summary: This is a funerary dedication by parents for their deceased son, who was 23 years old, likely from the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08000645.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Decimus Apronius Caricus made this for his dearest wife, Apronia Marcella, who served him well, and for himself and his descendants while alive.
EDCS-08000645.summary: This is a funerary inscription by a husband for his wife and for himself and his descendants, likely dating to the 2nd or 3rd century CE.

EDCS-08000646.translation: Marcus Bittius Baraco, son of Marcus, is buried here. Age 9 years. Marcus Bitt[ius ---]
EDCS-08000646.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a young boy named Marcus Bittius Baraco, who died at age nine, likely from the imperial period.

EDCS-08000648.translation: To the divine shades. Lucretia Lysistrates. Aemilia Cratia, the mother, and Bilenius Onesimus, the husband, made this for their most devoted daughter, aged 22.
EDCS-08000648.summary: This is a tombstone inscription honoring Lucretia Lysistrates, erected by her mother and husband.

EDCS-08000649.translation: For Licinia Polla, daughter of Gaius. Licinia Secunda, daughter of Gaius, her mother, made this for her most dutiful daughter while alive.
EDCS-08000649.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Licinia Polla, erected by her mother.

EDCS-08000650.translation: For Maia Paternus, daughter of Marcus, aged 11. Her parents [made this] for their most devoted daughter.
EDCS-08000650.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Maia Paternus, erected by her parents.

EDCS-08000651.translation: Lucius Minicius Genethlius made this for his dear and most dutiful wife, Minicia Lycoris. I ask you, passerby, to say: May the earth be light upon you.
EDCS-08000651.summary: This is a tombstone inscription honoring Minicia Lycoris, erected by her husband Lucius Minicius Genethlius.

EDCS-08000652.translation: For Pompeia Nicenus, aged 25. Manius Lucretius Trophimus made this for his most dutiful wife.
EDCS-08000652.summary: This is a tombstone inscription honoring Pompeia Nicenus, erected by her husband Manius Lucretius Trophimus.

EDCS-08000655.translation: To Sentrus, son of Adreitus. Gaius Albicus, son of Gaius Exomnacius Rufus Octavius, son of Gaius Exomnacius, made this for himself and for his own.
EDCS-08000655.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Sentrus, son of Adreitus, erected by Gaius Albicus Exomnacius Rufus Octavius.

EDCS-08000657.translation: To the divine shades. Apronia Felicitas made this for her husband Quintus Vettius Mansuetus, who deserved well.
EDCS-08000657.summary: This is a tombstone inscription honoring Quintus Vettius Mansuetus, erected by his wife Apronia Felicitas.

EDCS-08000660.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely records a person's name and age.

EDCS-08000662.translation: To the divine shades. Nonieca[---] daughter of [---] a virgin [---]
EDCS-08000662.summary: This is a fragmentary tombstone inscription that names Nonieca and mentions she was a virgin.

EDCS-08000663.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that mentions the name Aretosa and the concept of memory.

EDCS-08000799.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Lucius Monninus Eticus. Monnina [restores the dedication].
EDCS-08000799.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Lucius Monninus Eticus by Monnina.

EDCS-08000802.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Kaniniae Gai filiae Catullae Atimetus bene merenti\n
EDCS-08000802.translation: To the spirits of the departed. To Kaninia, daughter of Gaius, called Catulla. Atimetus [erected this] for her, who deserved well.
EDCS-08000802.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Kaninia Catulla by Atimetus.

EDCS-08000803.summary: This inscription is fragmentary and likely funerary, with names and possibly an age.

EDCS-08100001.text_edition: \n Lucio Calusio Marco tribuno cohortis primae Flaviae Seconia Vera filio karissimo\n
EDCS-08100001.translation: To Lucius Calusius Marcus, tribune of the First Flavian Cohort, Seconia [dedicated this to her] dearest son.
EDCS-08100001.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Lucius Calusius Marcus, a tribune in the military, likely erected by his mother Seconia.

EDCS-08100002.translation: To Sextus Aemilius, son of Sextus, of the Voltinia tribe, a soldier of the Ninth Legion.
EDCS-08100002.summary: This inscription records Sextus Aemilius, a soldier of the Ninth Legion.

EDCS-08100005.translation: [...]. Secundus, curator of the college of builders and the centonarii of the colony Augusta Mediolanum Titiana, [received X m] via the centuria, from the will of [Didia] Prima, his wife.
EDCS-08100005.summary: This inscription details the funerary arrangements and endowment for Secundus, a curator of trade guilds in Mediolanum.

EDCS-08100006.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Marcus Kaninius Severus, who lived 14 years, 8 months, and 8 days. In memory of him, Marcus Kaninius [ Severus?] and Patinia Sabina, parents, [erected this] for their dearest son, and for Statia Paulina.
EDCS-08100006.summary: This is a funerary monument erected by parents for their son Marcus Kaninius Severus, and also for Statia Paulina.

EDCS-08100011.text_edition: \n Lucius Laivius sic Clemens miles legionis XV Apollinaris merito votum solvit libens\n
EDCS-08100011.translation: Lucius Laivius Clemens, a soldier of the Fifteenth Apollinaris Legion, fulfilled his vow willingly and deservedly.
EDCS-08100011.summary: This is a votive inscription by Lucius Laivius Clemens, a soldier of the Fifteenth Apollinaris Legion.

EDCS-08100014.translation: Of Marcus Valerius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, soldier.
EDCS-08100014.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription recording a soldier named Marcus Valerius.

EDCS-08100016.translation: [... as]edile, quaestor, duumvir with jurisdiction. Patron of the college [...], by the will of Didia Prima, his wife.
EDCS-08100016.summary: This inscription details funerary arrangements and honors for a man who held various civic and potentially collegial offices, established by his wife Didia Prima.

EDCS-08100019.translation: Memmia Maxsuma, daughter of Sextus, wife of a six-man board of Augustales priests.
