EDCS-08100019.summary: This inscription records the wife of a prominent local magistrate and priest, likely from the early imperial period.

EDCS-08100020.translation: Gaius Aemilius Florus, son of Spurius, of the Camilia tribe, and Publius Aemilius, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe.
EDCS-08100020.summary: This inscription names two individuals, likely citizens of the same family and tribe, possibly on a funerary monument.

EDCS-08100021.translation: Marcus Allius Secundus, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, made this while alive for himself and for his wife Viccia Tertulla, daughter of Quintus, aged 10 years.
EDCS-08100021.summary: This funerary inscription records a man who built a tomb for himself and his wife, specifying her young age at death.

EDCS-08100022.translation: Arcelaus, freedman of a woman, for himself and for Vettia Albana, freedwoman of Sextus, his living consort.
EDCS-08100022.summary: This is a funerary inscription for a freedman and his deceased female partner (contubernalis).

EDCS-08100023.translation: Gaius Attilius, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, made this while alive for himself and for [his wife/family].
EDCS-08100023.summary: This funerary inscription records a man who built a tomb for himself and likely his family.

EDCS-08100024.translation: Lucius Attius Stabilio, son of Lucius, aged 32 years.
EDCS-08100024.summary: This funerary inscription records a man named Lucius Attius Stabilio and his age at death.

EDCS-08100026.translation: Lucius Attiolenus Belibaeus, freedman of Lucius Titius, and his wife Mevia Alla, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-08100026.summary: This inscription records a freedman and his wife, likely on a funerary monument.

EDCS-08100027.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide specific details, but likely records personal names.

EDCS-08100029.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide specific details, but likely records personal names.

EDCS-08100031.translation: Of Lucius Docconius, Do[---], VO[---], Docco[---], Rufin[us?].
EDCS-08100031.summary: This inscription is too fragmented to provide specific details, but likely records personal names, possibly related to a family or business.

EDCS-08100032.translation: Lucius Ennius Faustinus, freedman of Lucius.
EDCS-08100032.summary: This is a funerary epitaph identifying Lucius Ennius Faustinus, a freedman.

EDCS-08100034.translation: Gaius Helvius Felix, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, made this while alive for himself and his son Gaius Helvius. He lived 20 years. This monument will not pass to an heir. In the front 100 feet, in the field 120 feet.
EDCS-08100034.summary: A funerary epitaph for Gaius Helvius Felix, recording the dimensions of the plot and mentioning his deceased son and brother, likely dating to the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08100035.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Laeliae Titi libertae Secundae et Luci Alli Lamyri parentibus pientissimis Cornelia Titi filia Prepusa fecit\n
EDCS-08100035.translation: To the Divine Shades. Cornelia Prepusa, daughter of Titus, made this for her most devoted parents, Laelia Secunda, freedwoman of Titus, and Lucius Allius Lamyris.
EDCS-08100035.summary: A funerary dedication made by Cornelia Prepusa for her deceased parents, Laelia Secunda and Lucius Allius Lamyris.

EDCS-08100036.translation: To Memmia Tyche, freedwoman, 35 years old, Quintus Terentius Ianuarius for his well-deserving wife.
EDCS-08100036.summary: A funerary epitaph from Quintus Terentius Ianuarius for his wife, Memmia Tyche.

EDCS-08100040.summary: This is a simple funerary epitaph identifying Pollia Tertia.

EDCS-08100042.summary: A fragmentary inscription possibly mentioning a woman named Restituta and a man named Notus.

EDCS-08100045.translation: To Quintus Valerius, son of Gaius, of the Camilia tribe, who made this while alive. Reader, fare well.
EDCS-08100045.summary: A funerary epitaph for Quintus Valerius, likely erected by himself during his lifetime, with a farewell to the reader.

EDCS-08100048.translation: Marcus Vettius [son], of the Camilia tribe, made this while alive.
EDCS-08100048.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcus Vettius, who commissioned his own tomb.

EDCS-08100049.translation: To the Divine Shades. For Villia Sophes. Gaius Villius, her son.
EDCS-08100049.summary: A funerary dedication from Gaius Villius for his mother, Villia Sophes.

EDCS-08300304.summary: This appears to be a tombstone or dedication bearing the name Statius Marcius Lucifer.

EDCS-08300305.translation: To Gaius Curtuis, son of Caius.
EDCS-08300305.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Gaius Curtuis, son of Caius.

EDCS-08300306.translation: Here rests in peace Abbot Rufus, who departed on the 3rd day of [---].
EDCS-08300306.summary: This is a funerary inscription recording the death of Abbot Rufus.

EDCS-08300307.text_edition: \n Vivus fecit Cnaeus Pactumeius Titi filius Niger Publio Pactumeio Titi filio veterano nepoti \n
EDCS-08300307.translation: Gnaeus Pactumeius Niger, son of Titus, made this while alive for Publius Pactumeius, son of Titus, a veteran, and his nephew.
EDCS-08300307.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Gnaeus Pactumeius Niger for his nephew.

EDCS-08300308.translation: Eliona, daughter of Lucius, a Prisca.
EDCS-08300308.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Eliona, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-08300311.text_edition: \n Quintus Didius Quinti filius posuit titulum sibi et filio suo Caio Didio Quinti filio Tromentina Primo veterano Quinto Didio Cai filio patri Valeriae Cai filiae Primae \n
EDCS-08300311.translation: Quintus Didius, son of Quintus, set up this tombstone for himself, his son Gaius Didius, son of Quintus, a veteran of the Tromentina tribe, for Primo, for his father Quintus Didius, son of Gaius, and for his daughter Valeria Prima, daughter of Gaius.
EDCS-08300311.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Quintus Didius for himself and his family members, including his father and son who was a veteran.

EDCS-08400240.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Felicitatis Quinta Octaviae Lucanae vernae suae fecit vixit anno I mensibus VIII diebus XXV sit tibi terra levis\n
EDCS-08400240.translation: To the Divine Manes. Felicitas, a slave girl of Octavia Lucana, made this for her. She lived for 1 year, 8 months, and 25 days. May the earth lie lightly on you.
EDCS-08400240.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Felicitas, a slave, set up by her owner, recording her lifespan.

EDCS-08400241.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Marco Lollio Heliodoro vixit annis II mensibus V diebus XX fecerunt Titus Flavius Eutychus et Flavia Cerine\n
EDCS-08400241.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. He lived for 2 years, 5 months, and 20 days. Titus Flavius Eutychus and Flavia Cerine made this.
EDCS-08400241.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for an unnamed individual, recording their lifespan and the names of those who set it up.

EDCS-08400242.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus sacrum Luci Mummi Restituti Pilia Psaechas coniugi suo cum quo vixit annis XL\n
EDCS-08400242.translation: Sacred to the Divine Manes. Pilia Psaechas for her husband Lucius Mummius Restitutus, with whom she lived for 40 years.
EDCS-08400242.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lucius Mummius Restitutus, set up by his wife Pilia Psaechas, recording the duration of their marriage.

EDCS-08400243.text_edition: \n Lucius Octavius Urbicus sibi et Octaviae Syntycheni uxori suae et suis vivus fecit\n
EDCS-08400243.translation: Lucius Octavius Urbicus made this while alive for himself, for his wife Octavia Syntyche, and for his [other] family members.
EDCS-08400243.summary: This is a funerary inscription made by Lucius Octavius Urbicus for himself, his wife, and other family members.

EDCS-08400244.text_edition: \n Statoria Marci filia Quarta Caius Statorius Sippo Manilia Mani filia Tertulla Statoriae Cai filiae Appiae annorum XXII Caio Statorio Proculo filio nnorum XXV\n
EDCS-08400244.translation: Statoria, daughter of Marcus, Quarta. Gaius Statorius Sippo. Manilia Tertulla, daughter of Manius. For Statoria Appia, daughter of Gaius, aged 22 years. For Gaius Statorius Proculus, aged 25 years.
EDCS-08400244.summary: This is a funerary inscription listing several individuals, including Statoria Appia and Gaius Statorius Proculus, with their ages and family connections.

EDCS-08400245.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Symposio Pamphilo filio bene merenti mater et soror fecerunt qui vixit annos XXIX menses VIIII\n
EDCS-08400245.translation: To the Divine Spirits. His mother and sister made this for Symposius Pamphilus, their deserving son, who lived 29 years and 9 months.
EDCS-08400245.summary: A funerary epitaph for Symposius Pamphilus, erected by his mother and sister, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-08400246.text_edition: \n Caio Trassario Cai filio Restituto Dertona militi cohortis X praetoriae centuria Proculi militavit nnos XV vixit nnos XXXV heres faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-08400246.translation: To Gaius Trassarius Restitutus, son of Gaius, of Dertona, a soldier of the 10th praetorian cohort, in the century of Proculus. He served 15 years and lived 35 years. His heir had this made.
EDCS-08400246.summary: A military epitaph for Gaius Trassarius Restitutus, detailing his service in the Praetorian Guard and his lifespan, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-08400248.translation: Of good memory, Petrus. Lived more than 50 years. Rested in peace.
EDCS-08400248.summary: A short epitaph for Petrus, indicating his age at death and his peaceful repose, probably from late antiquity.

EDCS-08400250.translation: Calos, son of Actius, from Castra.
EDCS-08400250.summary: A very brief inscription identifying a person named Calos and his origin, possibly a tombstone or a property marker.

EDCS-08400253.text_edition: \n io Marci filio rioni Saturninae rae Hic`requiescit ? Archadius! ssis \n
EDCS-08400253.translation: [---] son of Marcus, [---]oninus Saturnina [---]. Here rests? Archadius! [---]
EDCS-08400253.summary: A fragmented epitaph that mentions individuals named Marcus, Saturnina, and Archadius, likely from the late Roman period, with difficulties in full interpretation.

EDCS-08400572.translation: To Lucius Talicius Pisonius, son of Marcus, of the Publician tribe, IIIIvir. Titus Virius, son of Gnaeus, of the Publician tribe. Marcus Virius, son of Titus, of the Publician tribe.
EDCS-08400572.summary: A dedication to Lucius Talicius Pisonius, a magistrate, with the names of two other individuals, Titus Virius and Marcus Virius, likely from an honorific monument in the Republican or early Imperial period.

EDCS-08600252.text_edition: \n condedit sic tia Severiana hoc funeri sic dolens quod mihi debuerant fecisse sic ego mater scelesta feci nti parvoli sic loci \n
EDCS-08600252.translation: Severiana established this tombstone; grieving that they owed me what they should have done, I, the wretched mother, made this for the child of the place.
EDCS-08600252.summary: A deeply personal and sorrowful epitaph from a mother for her child, lamenting her own perceived failings and dedicating the monument, possibly from late antiquity.

EDCS-08600253.translation: I adjure any mortal that no one may remove this memorial or place another in this memorial, if you do not have a share with Judas the traitor.
EDCS-08600253.summary: A curse inscription intended to protect a burial place, warning against disturbing the grave and invoking a negative comparison with Judas, likely from the early Christian period.

EDCS-08600256.text_edition: \n Iovi Optimo Maximo s Marci filius Ingenus sic Delphus \n
EDCS-08600256.translation: To Jupiter Optimus Maximus. Marcus son of Ingenus Delphus.
EDCS-08600256.summary: A dedication to Jupiter Optimus Maximus by Marcus Ingenus Delphus, possibly related to a votive offering or public benefit, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08600257.translation: Nicus Roncarius, son of Dissius, decurion.
EDCS-08600257.summary: An inscription identifying Nicus Roncarius, son of Dissius, as a decurion, likely a local official in a town or colony, from the Imperial period.

EDCS-08900380.translation: Quintus Cassius Callistus set this up for Mars.
EDCS-08900380.summary: This is a dedication to the god Mars by Quintus Cassius Callistus.

EDCS-09401420.translation: Titus Hortensius Probatus, an urban plebeian.
EDCS-09401420.summary: This inscription likely marks a tomb or dedication related to Titus Hortensius Probatus, identified as an urban plebeian.

EDCS-09401421.translation: Given as a gift to Fadiai Hesperis.
EDCS-09401421.summary: This records a gift given to someone named Fadiai Hesperis.

EDCS-09500013.translation: Lived and made. Caius Didius Vicarius, freedman of a woman, for himself and for Didia Prisca, daughter of Caius, his patroness, and for Didia Restituta, freedwoman of a woman, daughter, aged 19, and for Lucius Viccanius Apollonius, freedman of Lucius, his son-in-law. In the front 27 feet, in the field 19 feet. This monument will not pass to an heir.
EDCS-09500013.summary: This is a funerary monument inscription for Caius Didius Vicarius and his family, including measurements and a clause about inheritance, likely from the 1st or 2nd century CE.

EDCS-09500015.translation: Terentia Photis, freedwoman of Caius, [for herself and] A[---] CATV[---] P[---] CATV[---]
EDCS-09500015.summary: This fragmented funerary inscription seems to record Terentia Photis, a freedwoman, and possibly other individuals with the cognomen Catuvus.

EDCS-09500026.translation: Lucius Naevius Montanus, son of Lucius, of the Camilia tribe, lived and made.
EDCS-09500026.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Naevius Montanus, stating he built his own tomb while alive.

EDCS-10301350.translation: ] the place of Veneriosus the doorkeeper, who lived about 70 years, died on the 8th day before the Kalends of March [---], in the third consulship of Aetius and Symmachus.
EDCS-10301350.summary: This inscription records the burial place and lifespan of a doorkeeper named Veneriosus, dated by the consulship of Aetius and Symmachus.

EDCS-10301352.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace Taurus the little one, who lived eight years and 30 days, died on the 4th Ides of March, after the consulship of Aetius thrice and Symmachus, most illustrious men.
EDCS-10301352.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for a young child named Taurus, providing his age at death and the date, which is given by the consulship of Aetius and Symmachus.

EDCS-10301358.translation: ] who lived [---] on the day before [---] here rests [---] Albinus the innocent, who lived in this world about 6 years, 6 months, and 15 days, died on the [---] Ides of July, when Simmacus was vir clarissimus, consul.
EDCS-10301358.summary: This funerary inscription records the death of a child named Albinus, specifying his age at death and the date by the consulship of Simmacus.

EDCS-10301359.translation: Here rests in peace Lea, who lived approximately 45 years, died on the 12th day before the Kalends of October, when Decius was vir clarissimus, consul.
EDCS-10301359.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Lea, stating her approximate age at death and the date based on the consulship of Decius.

EDCS-10301361.translation: To good memory. Here rests in peace Domnella, who lived about 60 years, departed on the 12th day before the Kalends of May, after the consulship of Paulinus, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-10301361.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Domnella, providing her lifespan and date of death relative to the consulship of Paulinus, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-10301363.translation: Here rests in peace Lumenosa, who lived about 36 years, departed on the Ides of June, under the consulship of Mavurtio, a most distinguished man.
EDCS-10301363.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lumenosa, stating her age at death and the consular dating of her passing, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-10301369.translation: To good memory. Here rests in peace Florianus, who lived about two years and three months, departed on the 16th day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-10301369.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Florianus, detailing his lifespan in years and months and the consular dating of his death, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-10301373.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph, possibly for an individual named Capr[---], that records a lifespan, the dating of which is lost.

EDCS-10301374.translation: [---] in this century [---] 2 years, 7 months, [---] Conan[---] dearest(?)
EDCS-10301374.summary: This is a fragmented inscription that likely commemorates a person named Conan[---], mentioning a lifespan of 2 years and 7 months, with some emotional sentiment.

EDCS-10301377.summary: This is a very fragmentary epitaph that begins to record the resting place in peace of an individual named El[---].

EDCS-10301380.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription, possibly part of a larger text that identified a person named John or related to him.

EDCS-10301381.translation: To good memory. Here rests in peace Lauricia, who lived about 9 years, departed on the 5th day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-10301381.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Lauricia, providing her approximate age at death and the consular dating of her passing, likely from the 4th or 5th century CE.

EDCS-10301382.summary: This is a fragment of an epitaph that begins to record the resting place of an individual named Leo.

EDCS-10301383.translation: [---] in the very place Lupula [---] who lived 40 years.
EDCS-10301383.summary: This is a fragmentary epitaph that mentions an individual named Lupula and records her lifespan as 40 years, possibly indicating a burial location.

EDCS-10301384.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace Marusa, who lived more or less 60 years. Died on the third day before the Kalends of September.
EDCS-10301384.summary: An epitaph recording the death and age of Marusa, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301388.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace Pricticius, who lived more or less 30 years and lived with his wife for [unknown number] years. Died on the tenth day before the Kalends of March.
EDCS-10301388.summary: An epitaph for Pricticius, detailing his lifespan and marital duration, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301390.translation: Here lies in peace Rusticus, who lived about [unknown number] years. Died in the fifth [year of an unknown cycle?].
EDCS-10301390.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for Rusticus, mentioning his lifespan and a dating element, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301464.translation: Here rests in peace Abbot Rufinus, who died [unknown number]s. [Lacuna]
EDCS-10301464.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for an Abbot Rufinus, recording his rest and likely death date, from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301491.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace Agnellus, who lived in the world more or less 50 years. He was buried on the Ides of March in the consulship of Opilio, a most distinguished man. Here also rests his father Constantius and his mother Ferriola.
EDCS-10301491.summary: An epitaph commemorating Agnellus, his parents Constantius and Ferriola, and dating the burial to the consulship of Opilio in the late Roman period.

EDCS-10301492.translation: Of good memory. Here rests in peace the venerable man, presbyter Bereuulfus, who lived in this world more or less 70 years. He rested on the third day before the Kalends of January. [Lacuna]
EDCS-10301492.summary: An epitaph for the presbyter Bereuulfus, stating his age and date of rest, likely from a monastic or church context in late antiquity.

EDCS-10301498.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace, of good memory, Agnella, who lived more or less 30 years and passed away on the Kalends of February in the fourth indiction.
EDCS-10301498.summary: An epitaph for Agnella, providing her age and date of death linked to an indiction cycle, typical of late Roman provincial inscriptions.

EDCS-10301499.translation: Here rests in peace Asteria, [who lived] more or less 55 years.
EDCS-10301499.summary: A fragmentary epitaph for Asteria, stating her age, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301501.translation: Here rests Rusticianos in the sleep of peace, and he lived eighty years in positions of power.
EDCS-10301501.summary: An epitaph for Rusticianos, noting his long life and presumably important status, from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301502.translation: Here rests Venerusa in the sleep of peace, who lived 86 years and passed away on the sixth day before the Kalends of June.
EDCS-10301502.summary: An epitaph for Venerusa, detailing her age and date of death, likely from late antiquity.

EDCS-10301518.translation: We designate as holy the names of Stephen, the protomartyr, John the Evangelist, Lawrence, Victor, Navor, Felix, Protasius, and Gervasius.
EDCS-10301518.summary: This inscription lists the names of several saints, likely for a reliquary or a church dedicated to them, possibly from the early medieval period.

EDCS-10301519.translation: The burial of Maiorianus, eight days before the Kalends of July. I adjure you by Christ not to open this place, Florentius, a man of clarissimate rank, being consul.
EDCS-10301519.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Maiorianus, dated by the consulship of Florentius, which includes an adjuration not to disturb the grave.

EDCS-10301520.translation: Buried on the eighth day before the Ides of May, in the consulship of Agapitus, a man of clarissimate rank, and Marina, who lived seven years, buried on the eighth day before the Kalends of November, in the consulships of Symmachus and Boethius, men of clarissimate rank. I adjure you by Christ not to open this place.
EDCS-10301520.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Agapitus and Marina, providing their ages and burial dates, and includes an adjuration against disturbing the tomb, dated by the consulships of Agapitus and the later pair Symmachus and Boethius.

EDCS-10301522.translation: Here rests in peace, of good memory, Maurianus, who lived in this world more or less four years, was buried on the Ides of April, in the fifteenth indiction, during the reign of our lord Emperor Mauritius, perpetual Augustus, in his fifteenth year.
EDCS-10301522.summary: This epitaph records the burial of Maurianus, who died at a young age, and provides the date of burial, the indiction, and the emperor's reign, likely from the late 6th or early 7th century.

EDCS-10301528.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that likely records the death or burial of a woman named Domitia.

EDCS-10301532.translation: Whoever enters this enclosure, if you care to know the place that rejoices and the members honored within this tomb, read this page of verse; Acilius taught. Here rests in peace, of good memory, Maria, coming from a noble lineage of parents, to whom only three years were permitted to be sweetly united with her husband, whom envious death deprived of her sweetness after completing the seventeenth year of her age. She was buried on the fourth day before the Kalends of January, in the fourteenth indiction.
EDCS-10301532.summary: This is a lengthy epitaph for Maria, detailing her noble lineage, short married life, and early death at seventeen, with the burial date and indiction provided, likely from the 4th or 5th century.

EDCS-10301543.translation: [Chresteanus(?)] [---] thirty-two years [---] [---] a most distinguished virgin man.
EDCS-10301543.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that seems to record the age and status of a person named Chresteanus, possibly a priest or a prominent individual.

EDCS-10301557.summary: This is a very fragmentary inscription that appears to be a memorial for a person named Charetosa.

EDCS-10301558.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that likely mentions a priest named Mutinus and his age.

EDCS-10700016.text_edition: \n Grattia Titi filia Restituta sibi et Marco Aponio Prisco VIviro Eporediae viro et Marco Aponio Restituto filio VIviro Eporediae aedili IIviro Industriae viva fecit\n
EDCS-10700016.translation: Grattia Restituta, daughter of Titus, made this for herself and for Marcus Aponius Priscus, VIvir of Eporedia, her husband, and for Marcus Aponius Restitutus, son of Marcus, VIvir of Eporedia and aedile and IIvir of Industriae, while she was alive.
EDCS-10700016.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Grattia Restituta for herself and her husband and son, who held various civic offices in Eporedia and Industriae, likely from the Roman Imperial period.

EDCS-10700017.inscription_type: inscriptiones christianae, tituli operum, tituli sepulcrales
EDCS-10700017.translation: This monument is for Chrysidis; her miserable parents placed it. Earth presses down her ashes, whose year of life was [ ]simus. She lies in this tomb.
EDCS-10700017.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Chrysidis, placed by her parents, dating to an uncertain period based on the incomplete age.

EDCS-10700018.translation: Salvius Cocceius, son of Gaius, from the Pollia tribe, erected this for Quarta Iovonia Tertia, daughter of Tertius.
EDCS-10700018.summary: This is a funerary dedication erected by Salvius Cocceius for Quarta Iovonia Tertia, likely from the imperial period given the naming conventions.

EDCS-10700020.translation: To the son of Gaius, [son] of Gnaeus Ruf[---].
EDCS-10700020.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication, with incomplete names and filiations.

EDCS-10700889.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Luci Caecili Alexandri coniugi bene merenti Caecilia Tyrannis\n
EDCS-10700889.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Caecilia Tyrannis set this up for her well-deserving husband, Lucius Caecilius Alexander.
EDCS-10700889.summary: This is a funerary epitaph dedicated by Caecilia Tyrannis to her husband, Lucius Caecilius Alexander, in the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10700890.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Decimo Petronio Decimi filio Stellatina Proculo vixit nnis XLV mense I diebus VIII horis VIIII Petronia Tyche patrono bene merenti fecit\n
EDCS-10700890.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. Petronia Tyche made this for her esteemed patron, Proculus, son of Decimus, of the Stellatina tribe, who lived 45 years, 1 month, 8 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-10700890.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Proculus, dedicated by his freedwoman Petronia Tyche, providing his age at death and dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10701280.text_edition: \n Matronis Publius Didius Callinicus votum solvit libens laetus\n
EDCS-10701280.translation: Publius Didius Callinicus gladly and joyfully paid his vow to the Matronae.
EDCS-10701280.summary: This is a dedication by Publius Didius Callinicus to the Matronae, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10701290.text_edition: \n Publius Didius Titi filius Camilia us\n
EDCS-10701290.translation: Publius Didius, son of Titus, of the Camilia tribe.
EDCS-10701290.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely an epitaph or a mention of citizenship, for Publius Didius of the Camilia tribe.

EDCS-10701296.text_edition: \n Dis Manibus Severae Chresimus conservae karissimae quae vixit nnos XXI\n
EDCS-10701296.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. For Severa, my dearest fellow slave, who lived 21 years.
EDCS-10701296.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Severa, dedicated by a fellow slave (conserva), dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10701297.text_edition: \n Decimo Sufenati Decimi filio Poblilia Acrippae sic Licinia mater\n
EDCS-10701297.translation: To Decimus Sufenatius, son of Decimus. Licinia his mother [placed this].
EDCS-10701297.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Decimus Sufenatius, erected by his mother Licinia, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-10701304.translation: Burial of Maiorianus, placed on the 8th day before the Kalends of July. I adjure [you] by Christ not to open this place, [to] Florentius, most illustrious man, consul.
EDCS-10701304.summary: This is a Christian funerary inscription from the Roman imperial period, warning against disturbing the burial of Maiorianus and mentioning the consul Florentius.

EDCS-10800280.translation: To Lucius Herennius, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe
EDCS-10800280.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription likely dedicating a monument to Lucius Herennius, identified by his father's name and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-10800285.translation: Optatus (?), his son, and Lucius, his son, have gladly and deservedly paid their vow.
EDCS-10800285.summary: This inscription records a vow paid by Optatus and his son Lucius, likely to a deity.

EDCS-10800290.summary: This is a simple funerary inscription identifying the deceased as Gaius Arius Avelanius.

EDCS-10800291.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription that appears to identify Lucius Helpidius, possibly from Antioch.

EDCS-10800292.summary: This inscription identifies Veconus Lulonius, the son of Carantus, likely a funerary or honorary text.

EDCS-10800293.translation: Disia, wife of Ulatunus, son of Dirco, and his son Enistalus [paid their vow?].
EDCS-10800293.summary: This inscription, though fragmented, seems to record members of a family, possibly fulfilling a vow, and includes at least one patronymic.

EDCS-10800297.translation: Lucius Crispius Augustinus, duumvir, gladly and deservedly paid his vow to the gods Rubascas and Robeon.
EDCS-10800297.summary: This inscription records Lucius Crispius Augustinus, a duumvir, paying a vow to the gods Rubascas and Robeon, likely during his term of office.

EDCS-10800302.translation: To the Divine Shades. Titus Attius Superus, son of Caius, made this for himself while alive, and for...
EDCS-10800302.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Titus Attius Superus, identified by his father's name, made provision for himself and others while alive.

EDCS-10800303.summary: This inscription is a very short dedication or statement by Quintus Caturlius.

EDCS-10800305.translation: To Veconus Costigenius, from Statannus, to Veconus.
EDCS-10800305.summary: This inscription appears to record a dedication or transfer of property, possibly from Statannus to Veconus, and mentions another Vecono.

EDCS-10800350.translation: Quartus Caprilius Verinus willingly and gladly paid his vow to Minerva for Caprilia Verina.
EDCS-10800350.summary: A votive inscription by Quartus Caprilius Verinus for Caprilia Verina, likely dedicated to Minerva.

EDCS-10800351.translation: Marcus Cassius, son of Marcus, father; Marcus Cassius, son of Marcus, son; from the Pollia tribe, centurion of the [legion --], for himself and his father.
EDCS-10800351.summary: A funerary inscription for Marcus Cassius and his son, a centurion, potentially dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10800352.translation: Caius Racilius Amphio, son of Caius, of the Palatine tribe, for himself and his wife and his children; Licinia Salvia; Caius Racilius; Lucius Racilius.
EDCS-10800352.summary: A funerary inscription for Caius Racilius Amphio, his wife, and children, likely dating to the late Republic or early Empire.

EDCS-10800353.summary: A simple funerary epitaph identifying Volta Tatia, a freedwoman, and her patron.

EDCS-10800354.translation: Ordered to be made by will; [---]ninus; [---] to Nino, father; [---]iae Rufae; [---] to Nino, brother.
EDCS-10800354.summary: A funerary inscription indicating that the monument was ordered by will for a father, mother, and brother, with lacunae obscuring specific names.

EDCS-10900019.text_edition: \n Publio Toranio Titi filio Pollia Secundo veterano legionis XIII patri Iuniae Marci filiae Primigeniae matri Torania Publi filia Prima viva fecit\n
EDCS-10900019.translation: To Publius Toranius Secundus, son of Titus, veteran of the 13th legion, father; to Iunia Primigenia, daughter of Marcus, mother. Made by Torania Prima, daughter of Publius, while alive.
EDCS-10900019.summary: A funerary monument erected by Torania Prima for her parents, Publius Toranius Secundus, a legionary veteran, and Iunia Primigenia.

EDCS-10900020.text_edition: \n Caius Silucius Marci filius Secundus IIIIIIvir sibi et Marco Silucio Marci filio Metello patri Tilloniae Cnaei filiae Alebinnae matri testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-10900020.translation: Caius Silucius Secundus, son of Marcus, a *IIIIvir*, for himself and for Marcus Silucius Metellus, son of Marcus, father; Tillonia Alebinna, daughter of Cnaeus, mother. Ordered to be made by will.
EDCS-10900020.summary: A funerary monument ordered by will for Caius Silucius Secundus, a *IIIIvir*, and his parents, Marcus Silucius Metellus and Tillonia Alebinna.

EDCS-10900021.text_edition: \n Collegium dendrophororum de pecunia sua scholam exornavit Marcus Septimius Argus locum dedit\n
EDCS-10900021.translation: The guild of dendrophori decorated the meeting hall with their own funds; Marcus Septimius Argus gave the site.
EDCS-10900021.summary: An inscription recording the decoration of a meeting hall by the dendrophori guild, with Marcus Septimius Argus donating the location.

EDCS-10900022.text_edition: \n Marco Milionio Thalasso Quintus Atilius Faustus maedagogus collegii fabrorum hermas\n
EDCS-10900022.translation: Quintus Atilius Faustus, a *maedagogus* of the guild of *fabri*, [dedicated/erected] herms to Marcus Milionius Thallasus.
EDCS-10900022.summary: An inscription recording the dedication of herms by Quintus Atilius Faustus, a *maedagogus* of the guild of *fabri*, to Marcus Milionius Thallasus.

EDCS-10900024.text_edition: \n Ategnatia Adgennis filia Secunda sibi et Persaeo Publi filio Tertio filio suo testamento fieri iussit\n
EDCS-10900024.translation: Ategnatia Adgennis Secunda, daughter of Adgennis, ordered to be made by will for herself and for her son Persaeus Tertius, son of Publius.
EDCS-10900024.summary: A funerary monument ordered by will by Ategnatia Adgennis Secunda for herself and her son, Persaeus Tertius.

EDCS-10900025.translation: To Lucius Campius Mansuetus, son of Lucius, of the Pollia tribe, patron, and for himself, Lucius Campius Privatus, freedman of Lucius, of the Palatina tribe, made (this) while alive.
EDCS-10900025.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by a freedman for his patron and himself, indicating the social relationships and tribal affiliations of the deceased.

EDCS-10900026.text_edition: \n Quintus Didius |(mulieris) libertus Savius sibi et Didiae Quinti libertae Helenae matri\n
EDCS-10900026.translation: Quintus Didius Savius, freedman of a woman, for himself and for Helena, freedwoman of Quintus Didius, his mother.
EDCS-10900026.summary: This inscription records a self-funded funerary monument for Quintus Didius Savius and his mother, Helena, highlighting familial and freedman status.

EDCS-10900027.translation: To the spirits of the underworld; Petronius Aepagathus (erected this) for his wife Licinia Irene.
EDCS-10900027.summary: This is a dedication to the 'dis manibus' (to the spirits of the underworld) for Licinia Irene, set up by her husband Petronius Aepagathus, indicating a standard funerary dedication.

EDCS-10900028.translation: Flavius, son of Publius, of the Pollia tribe, aged 20 years; Quarta, his mother, daughter of [Salvius?], of the family of Circenia(?); Publius Flavius, son of [Publius?], [erected this].
EDCS-10900028.summary: This is a funerary epitaph for Flavius, a 20-year-old man, with his mother and father identified, likely dating to the early imperial period based on naming conventions.

EDCS-10900029.translation: For himself and for his wife Laeva Paulina.
EDCS-10900029.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument established by an individual for himself and his wife, Laeva Paulina.

EDCS-10900030.summary: This is a fragment of an inscription identifying a woman named Martia, daughter of Lucius, likely part of a funerary or dedicatory text.

EDCS-10900032.translation: Secunda, his wife; Marcus Cocceius Felix, son of Marcus.
EDCS-10900032.summary: This fragmented inscription identifies Marcus Cocceius Felix and his wife Secunda, likely as part of a funerary monument or familial record.

EDCS-10900033.text_edition: \n optimi Secundina et sibi viva fecit\n
EDCS-10900033.translation: Secundina made (this) for the best (person/people) and for herself while alive.
EDCS-10900033.summary: This inscription records a funerary monument funded by Secundina for an unspecified 'best' individual or individuals, as well as for herself.

EDCS-10900034.translation: Spurius Verredius, son of Spurius, of the Pollia tribe, and Marcus Lucius, sons, made (this); Marcus Pe[---]
EDCS-10900034.summary: This funerary inscription records a monument made by two individuals, Spurius Verredius and Marcus Lucius, sons of Spurius and Marcus respectively, and names another individual partially.

EDCS-10900035.text_edition: \n Publius Villius Publi filius Popita Camilia annorum LXXV Caius Villius Publi filius annorum XXV\n
EDCS-10900035.translation: Publius Villius Popita, son of Publius, of the Camilia tribe, aged 75 years; Caius Villius, son of Publius, aged 25 years.
EDCS-10900035.summary: This epitaph records the names and ages of two individuals, Publius Villius Popita and Caius Villius, likely father and son, with tribal affiliation noted.

EDCS-10900039.summary: This inscription is a fragmentary dedication or epitaph mentioning the name Titus Perssius.

EDCS-10900040.translation: To Aesculapius, Quintus Dillius Iep[3]telus, a volunteer, gladly and deservedly, fulfilled his vow.
EDCS-10900040.summary: This is a votive inscription dedicated to Aesculapius by Quintus Dillius Ieptellus, who is fulfilling a vow.

EDCS-10900043.text_edition: \n Marci filius Faleria Bassus praefectus cohortis primae Antiochensium praefectus cohortis primae Brittonum praefectus alae Moesicae procurator Imperatoris Caesaris Traiani Hadriani Augusti ad XXXX Galliarum item ad censum agendum Ponto Bithyniae epistrategus Pelusio item Thebaidis procurator provinciae Iudaeae testamento poni iussit\n
EDCS-10900043.translation: Marcus Bassus, son of Marcus, of the Falernian tribe, prefect of the first cohort of Antiochenes, prefect of the first cohort of Britons, prefect of the ala of Moesia, procurator of the Emperor Caesar Trajan Hadrian Augustus for the province of Gaul with 40,000 denarii, also for the census in Pontus and Bithynia, epistrategus of Pelusium, also of the Thebaid, procurator of the province of Judaea, ordered this to be set up by his will.
EDCS-10900043.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by will for Marcus Bassus, a military officer and imperial procurator who served in various regions including Gaul, Pontus, Bithynia, Egypt, and Judaea, likely during the Hadrianic period.

EDCS-10900044.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Aemilius Secundinus made this for Aemilius Thelonicus for his merits.
EDCS-10900044.summary: This is a funerary dedication made by Aemilius Secundinus for Aemilius Thelonicus, honoring his merits.

EDCS-10900045.text_edition: \n Dis O Manibus bene merenti Aemiliae Marcellae F alumnae Novici\n
EDCS-10900045.translation: To the spirits of the departed, for the well-deserving Aemilia Marcella, the freedwoman of Novicius.
EDCS-10900045.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Aemilia Marcella, described as a well-deserving freedwoman, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-10900046.translation: To the spirits of the departed. Lucius Allius Ligus for himself, and for Valeria Thallusae, and for his most pious son Lucius Allius Allianus, aged 20 years.
EDCS-10900046.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Allius Ligus, his wife Valeria Thallusae, and their son Lucius Allius Allianus, who died at the age of 20, likely dating to the Imperial period.

EDCS-10900048.translation: To Quintus Calventius Severus. His mother, C. Calventius Manna, made this.
EDCS-10900048.summary: This is a funerary dedication for Quintus Calventius Severus, made by his mother, C. Calventia Manna.

EDCS-10900051.translation: To the spirits of the departed, sacred. Titus Flavius Tertius for Flavius Tertius his infant son and for himself with his family.
EDCS-10900051.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated by Titus Flavius Tertius for his infant son Flavius Tertius and for himself and his household.

EDCS-10900052.translation: To the spirits of the departed. For Iunia Marul[la
EDCS-10900052.summary: This is a fragmentary funerary dedication for Iunia Marulla.

EDCS-10900053.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription, likely a funerary dedication, for Licinia Amoena.

EDCS-10900054.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Nicomede, my dearest comrade in the barracks.
EDCS-10900054.summary: This is a funerary dedication to Nicomede, identified as a contubernalis (a soldier sharing a tent), likely set up by a loved one or family member.

EDCS-10900055.translation: To Porcia Tertia, daughter of Lucius, wife of Ligus. Lucius Asinius Ligus (erected this) to his wife.
EDCS-10900055.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Lucius Asinius Ligus to his wife, Porcia Tertia, mentioning her father and her name with a probable misspelling.

EDCS-10900057.translation: To Novicia, [---], to my deserving wife. Sextus S. [---] Ianuario (erected this).
EDCS-10900057.summary: This incomplete funerary inscription is a dedication to Novicia, identified as a wife, set up by Sextus S. Ianuario.

EDCS-10900058.translation: To Salvius Canuleius, son of Lucius, of the Aniensis tribe. Valeria Montana (erected this) to her husband.
EDCS-10900058.summary: This funerary dedication by Valeria Montana to her husband, Salvius Canuleius, includes his filiation and tribal affiliation.

EDCS-10900060.translation: To the spirits of the underworld. To Sextilia Patern(a), my most dutiful wife, who lived 29 years, 3 months, 5 days, and 9 hours.
EDCS-10900060.summary: This is a detailed funerary epitaph recording the age and lifespan of Sextilia Patern(a), dedicated to her by her husband.

EDCS-10900066.summary: This is a highly fragmented inscription that begins with the name Publius but provides no further context.

EDCS-10900068.summary: This is a fragmentary inscription mentioning the name Quintus, with no other discernible information.

EDCS-10900160.text_edition: \n Caio lio Poblilia Tessellae sic IIIIIIviro Calpurniae Titi filiae Priscae \n
EDCS-10900160.translation: To Gaius Ilius, tessellarius (mosaic worker) and viovir of Poblilia. To Calpurnia Prisca, daughter of Titus.
EDCS-10900160.summary: This inscription seems to be a dedication or record related to Gaius Ilius, a tessellarius and viovir, and Calpurnia Prisca.

EDCS-10900161.text_edition: \n Vivi fecerunt Publius Albius Marci filius Publilia Pateasus Albia Octavi filia Veltona uxor\n
EDCS-10900161.translation: Publius Albius, son of Marcus, and Albia Octavi filia Veltona, wife of the son of Publius, erected (this).
EDCS-10900161.summary: This inscription records the makers of a monument: Publius Albius and Albia Veltona, identifying their parentage and relationship.

EDCS-10900162.translation: To Marcus Aticius, son of Marcus.
EDCS-10900162.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a dedication or part of a longer text, identifying Marcus Aticius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-10900163.text_edition: \n Publi Betuti Cai fili annorum XXXV\n
EDCS-10900163.translation: Publius Betutius, son of Gaius, aged 35.
EDCS-10900163.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Publius Betutius, who died at the age of 35.

EDCS-10900164.text_edition: \n Lucio Papirio Publi filio Poblilia Bitironi\n
EDCS-10900164.translation: To Lucius Papirius, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, from Biturō.
EDCS-10900164.summary: This is a dedication to Lucius Papirius, son of Publius, belonging to the Poblilia tribe.

EDCS-10900165.translation: Terentius, son of [---], of the Poblilia tribe, Cinus.
EDCS-10900165.summary: This inscription names Terentius, son of [---], of the Poblilia tribe.

EDCS-10900166.text_edition: \n Lucius Terentius Publi filius Poblilia Varro et Valeria Marci filia Tertia\n
EDCS-10900166.translation: Lucius Terentius, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, and Valeria, daughter of Marcus, Tertia.
EDCS-10900166.summary: This inscription records the names Lucius Terentius and Valeria, daughter of Marcus, possibly a couple from the Poblilia tribe.

EDCS-10900167.text_edition: \n Lucius Valerius Publi filius Publilia vivus fecit sibi et Valerio filio Publilia\n
EDCS-10900167.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Publius, of the Poblilia tribe, alive, made this for himself and for his son Valerius, of the Poblilia tribe.
EDCS-10900167.summary: This is a funerary monument set up by Lucius Valerius for himself and his son Valerius.

EDCS-10900168.translation: To Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, [...]
EDCS-10900168.summary: This inscription begins a dedication to Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus.

EDCS-10900169.translation: [---] Valerius, son of Titus, son of Mat[---]
EDCS-10900169.summary: This fragment names Valerius, son of Titus, of an uncertain family branch.

EDCS-10900171.text_edition: \n Marcus Valerius Marci filius Publilia Secundus sibi et Valeriae Marci filiae Pollae uxori\n
EDCS-10900171.translation: Marcus Valerius, son of Marcus, of the Poblilia tribe, Secundus, for himself and for Valeria, daughter of Marcus, Polla, his wife.
EDCS-10900171.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Valerius Secundus for himself and his wife Valeria Polla.

EDCS-10900172.translation: Salvius Valerius, son of Titus, Super.
EDCS-10900172.summary: This inscription records the name Salvius Valerius, son of Titus.

EDCS-10900173.translation: Titus Vocontius, son of Titus, Iucundus, lived 15 years.
EDCS-10900173.summary: This is a tombstone inscription for Titus Vocontius Iucundus, who died at the age of 15.

EDCS-10900174.text_edition: \n Marci Voconi Marci filii Publilia Marcelli \n
EDCS-10900174.translation: Of Marcus Voconi, son of Marcus, of the Voltinian tribe, Marcellus.
EDCS-10900174.summary: A funerary epitaph for Marcellus, son of Marcus Voconi, likely dating from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11600090.translation: To Laria Chrysodice. Titus Larius Dionysius [dedicated this] to his most excellent freedwoman.
EDCS-11600090.summary: A funerary dedication from Titus Larius Dionysius to his freedwoman, Laria Chrysodice.

EDCS-11600091.translation: To the departed spirits. To Eutactus, VIvir, from Dertona. Caius Arruntius Meleager, his colleague, helper, manager, and dispenser for the college of Dertona, [dedicated this] to his well-deserving colleague. Caius Arruntius [and his] son, [dedicated this] to him.
EDCS-11600091.summary: A funerary dedication from colleagues and a son to Caius Arruntius Meleager, a VIvir from Dertona, likely dating from the 1st to 3rd century CE.

EDCS-11600092.translation: Here rests [in good memory] Cla..., who lived approximately 32 years, departed on the day before the Kalends of May in the consulship of our lord Julius Majorian.
EDCS-11600092.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the death of 'Cla...' who lived approximately 32 years and died before the Kalends of May during the consulship of Julius Majorian (458 CE).

EDCS-11600094.translation: To Lucius Albinus Optatus, son of Lucius. Vibia (?), daughter of Lucius.
EDCS-11600094.summary: A funerary epitaph for Lucius Albinus Optatus, son of Lucius, with a mention of Vibia.

EDCS-11600095.translation: To Cornelia, daughter of Lucius, of the [family name] Q...
EDCS-11600095.summary: An incomplete funerary epitaph for Cornelia, daughter of Lucius.

EDCS-11600096.translation: Paconia Celsa, daughter of Quintus, aged 18 years.
EDCS-11600096.summary: A funerary epitaph for Paconia Celsa, aged 18.

EDCS-11600097.translation: His sons and living Flavia Salvia, daughter of Caius, and living Caius Vennius Super, son of Caius, and living Lucius Vennius Secundus, son of Caius, and living Caius Vennius Quartus, son of Caius, [erected this] to Caius Vennius Maximus, son of Rufus, [and to] living Vennius Tertulla, his sister, [providing] 30 feet in front and 30 feet in area.
EDCS-11600097.summary: A funerary monument inscription recording the erection of a tomb by sons for their father, Caius Vennius Maximus, and their sister, Vennius Tertulla, specifying dimensions of the plot.

EDCS-11600100.translation: Caius Piranus Primus made [this]. Caius Piranus Philomusus made [this].
EDCS-11600100.summary: An inscription recording the construction of a monument by Caius Piranus Primus and Caius Piranus Philomusus.

EDCS-12300359.inscription_type: diplomata militaria, tituli operum, tituli sacri
EDCS-12300359.translation: Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, and Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, [the names of the soldiers who // on the 6th day before the Ides of January, when the Emperors Valerian Augustus (cos. II) and Gallienus Augustus were consuls, [Cohort I Praetoria Valeriana Galliena Pia Vindex], to Publius Annius Probus, son of Publius, of the Papirian tribe, from Poetovio, [enrolled and recognized // Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Valerianus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul for the 2nd time, and Emperor Caesar Publius Licinius Egnatius Gallienus Pius Felix Augustus, pontifex maximus, holding tribunician power for the 2nd time, consul, the names of the soldiers who served in the ten Praetorian cohorts, Valerian and Gallienan, the Pious and the Victorious, who served faithfully and bravely, we grant the right of marriage, but only with a single, first wife, so that even if they have married women of peregrine status, they may nevertheless have children as if born of two Roman citizens, on the day before the Ides of January, when the Emperors Valerian Augustus (cos. II) and Gallienus Augustus were consuls, Cohort I Praetoria Valeriana Galliena Pia Vindex, to Publius Annius Probus, son of Publius, of the Papirian tribe, from Poetovio, enrolled and recognized from a bronze tablet which is fixed on the wall in Rome behind the temple of the divine Augustus near the Minervas // Of Marcus Aurelius Quintianus, Of Lucius Aurelius Simplex, Of Publius Appius Marcellinus, Of Caius Coelius Germanicinus, Of Publius Aelius Bassanus, Of Marcus Aurelius Magrinus, Of Publius Bellicius Vicens.
EDCS-12300359.summary: A military diploma dating to January 3rd, 57 CE, granting the right of legal marriage to auxiliary soldiers of the Praetorian Cohorts Valeriana Galliena, listing the names of officers and recipients, and specifying it is inscribed from a bronze tablet in Rome.

EDCS-12800344.translation: To Calidius Eutyches, dearest man, who lived with his wife for 21 years and 3 days. Statius Euangelis, his wife, for one who deserved well, in peace.
EDCS-12800344.summary: This funerary inscription is a dedication by a wife to her deceased husband, noting his age and years of marriage.

EDCS-12800374.summary: This is a very short inscription, likely a name from a tombstone or monument, belonging to Gaius Vibius Colianus.

EDCS-13200282.translation: Capitonius Bassus, son of Marcus, of the Camilia tribe, soldier, standard-bearer of the XV Apollinaris Legion, ordered this to be made by his will; his heirs carried it out.
EDCS-13200282.summary: This inscription records a soldier, Capitonius Bassus, who served as a standard-bearer in the XV Apollinaris Legion and arranged for his monument in his will.

EDCS-13302512.text_edition: \n Marcus Lucretius Marci libertus Palatina Chrestus merkator sic vinarius testamento fieri iussit pedes quadrati XV\n
EDCS-13302512.translation: Marcus Lucretius Chrestus, freedman of Marcus, of the Palatina tribe, wine merchant, ordered this to be made by his will, covering 15 square feet.
EDCS-13302512.summary: This inscription records a wine merchant, Marcus Lucretius Chrestus, who commissioned his monument by will and specified its size.

EDCS-13302721.translation: The dust of Aurelius Prudentis Clementis, a good poet.
EDCS-13302721.summary: This brief inscription commemorates Aurelius Prudentis Clementis, identified as a poet of good character.

EDCS-13400243.text_edition: \n vicia Dis Manibus coniugi merenti Sexto S Ianuario\n
EDCS-13400243.translation: To the Divine Shades, for a wife who deserved well, Sextus S. Ianuarius.
EDCS-13400243.summary: This is a funerary inscription dedicated to Sextus S. Ianuarius, described as a deserving husband.

EDCS-13600039.translation: Sextus Atilius, son of Caius. Caius Atilius, son of Caius, of the Stellatina tribe. Sextus Atilius, son of Caius, of the Sergia tribe.
EDCS-13600039.summary: This inscription lists three individuals, likely family members, with their names, patronymics, and tribal affiliations, possibly from a tomb or family monument.

EDCS-13600040.summary: This is an incomplete inscription, likely the beginning of a name or dedication, belonging to someone named Cintullus.

EDCS-13600041.translation: Disius Pramanius Moccus, son of Moccus. Ena, wife. They ordered the monument to be made.
EDCS-13600041.summary: This inscription records Disius Pramanius Moccus and his wife Ena, who commissioned a monument, possibly a tombstone.

EDCS-13600042.translation: Valius made this for himself and for Vibius, his brother, a soldier, while alive.
EDCS-13600042.summary: This is a funerary inscription where Valius, while alive, commissioned a monument for himself and his brother Vibius, who was a soldier.

EDCS-13600043.summary: A funerary epitaph for Vibia Tertia, daughter of Gaius, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13600044.translation: Titus Villius Veco, son of Lucius, [for] himself and
EDCS-13600044.summary: The beginning of an inscription, likely a funerary monument, for Titus Villius Veco, son of Lucius, and possibly others, dating to the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13600045.translation: Maxsuma, formerly of [Publius] Louticinius, son of Marcus, [from]
EDCS-13600045.summary: The beginning of an inscription, likely funerary, mentioning a woman named Maxsuma and Publius Louticinius, son of Marcus, probably from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-13600047.translation: If you who read this wish to know the name of the deceased, here rests in good memory [a woman], an honorable woman who lived in this age more or less 53 years; her burial was on the 12th day before the Kalends of December, in the year of the consulship of the most illustrious man [---], the third consulship.
EDCS-13600047.summary: A funerary epitaph recording the burial of an honorable woman who lived approximately 53 years, with the date of burial and the consulship partially preserved, likely from the late Roman period.

EDCS-13600049.translation: Here rests in the sleep of peace Valentinianus, who lived 13 years and [X] months, and was buried on the day before the Kalends of March, in the year of the consulship of the most illustrious Probinus.
EDCS-13600049.summary: A funerary epitaph for Valentinianus, who died at the age of 13 years and some months, buried on the day before the Kalends of March, during the consulship of Probinus, dating to the late Roman Empire.

EDCS-13900604.text_edition: \n Lucio Castricio Marci filio Pomptina decurioni Priscus filius faciendum curavit\n
EDCS-13900604.translation: Priscus, son of Lucio Castricio, son of Marcus, of the Pomptina tribe, a decurion, had this made.
EDCS-13900604.summary: A funerary monument dedicated by Priscus to his father, Lucio Castricio, son of Marcus, a decurion of the Pomptina tribe, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-14100303.summary: The fragmented remnants of an inscription, likely a funerary epitaph, mentioning Cassius Secundus, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-14100305.translation: Monument for Titus Decimius, son of Titus(?), and for Vibia Felicia, freedwoman of Marcus, his wife, and for Decimia Vitalis, daughter of Titus. A monument for the sake of the family, little for the sake of piety. The monument's location: 12 feet in front, 24 feet in the ground.
EDCS-14100305.summary: A funerary monument erected by Titus Decimius for his wife Vibia Felicia and daughter Decimia Vitalis, providing dimensions of the plot, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-14100310.summary: A fragmented inscription, possibly funerary, mentioning Secunda, daughter of Marcus, from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-15700144.text_edition: \n Fortunae Meliori Marcus Vindius Verianus praefectus classis Flaviae Moesicae et a militiis III dono dedit\n
EDCS-15700144.translation: Marcus Vindius Verianus, prefect of the Flavian fleet in Moesia and of the three military commands, gave this as a gift to Fortuna Melior.
EDCS-15700144.summary: A dedication to the goddess Fortuna Melior by Marcus Vindius Verianus, prefect of the Flavian Moesian fleet and holder of three military commands, likely from the Roman imperial period.

EDCS-15900382.translation: Gaius Julius Ianuarius made this in Dertona.
EDCS-15900382.summary: This is a dedication by Gaius Julius Ianuarius in Dertona, likely related to a building or public work.

EDCS-16900056.text_edition: \n Lucius Ulattius Publi filius Lucius Valerius decreto decurionum cameras pavimenta tectum fecerunt Lucius Valerius Marci filius curator probavit\n
EDCS-16900056.translation: Lucius Valerius, son of Lucius, and Lucius Valerius, son of Marcus, curator, approved the construction of rooms, pavements, and a roof by Lucius Ulattius, son of Publius.
EDCS-16900056.summary: This inscription records the construction of rooms, pavements, and a roof, approved by a curator and carried out by Lucius Valerius, with Lucius Ulattius as the builder.

EDCS-20000142.translation: Quintus, son of Quintus, Rufus, and Marcus, son of Quintus, Rufus, after judging disputes between the people of Genuateis and Veiturios on the spot and settling their controversies, decreed that they should make boundaries and set up boundary stones where these had been made, and ordered them to come to Rome. In Rome, under the consulship of Lucius Caecilius, son of Quintus, and Quintus Mucius, son of Quintus, on the IDES OF DECEMBER, they gave sentence by decree of the Senate regarding the private land of the castellum of Vituriorum, which land they may sell and their heir may inherit, and that this land should not be subject to tax. The boundaries of the private land of the Langates are from the lowest stream which rises from the spring in Mannicelo to the river Edem, where the boundary stone is; from there upstream along the river to the river Lemurim; from there upstream along the river Lemurim to the stream Comberanea; from there upstream along the stream Comberanea to the valley Caeptiemam, where two boundary stones stand on either side of the Postumian road; from these boundary stones in a straight line to the stream Vendupale; from the stream Vindupale to the river Neviasca; from the river Neviasca upstream along its ridge to the river Procobera; from the river Procobera downstream to the stream Vinelascam; there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the stream Vinelesca, where a boundary stone stands near the Postumian road; from there another boundary stone stands across the Postumian road; from that boundary stone which stands across the Postumian road, in a straight line to the spring in Manicelum; from there downstream along the stream which rises from the spring in Manicelo to the boundary stone which stands at the river Edem. The public land which the Langenses possess, where the Edus and Procobera meet, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the river Edus to the lowest part of Mount Lemurino, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge of Mount Lemurino, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge of Lemurino, there a boundary stone stands on the mountain near the cave; from there upstream along the straight ridge to Mount Lemurinum, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge to the castellum which is called Alianus, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge to Mount Ioventionem, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge to Mount Apenninum which is called Boplo, there a boundary stone stands; from there along the ridge of the Apenninum to Mount Tuledonem, there a boundary stone stands; from there downstream along the straight ridge to the river Veraglascam, to the lowest part of Mount Berigiemam, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge to Mount Prenicum, there a boundary stone stands; from there along the ridge to the river Tulelascam, there a boundary stone stands; from there upstream along the straight ridge to Blustiemelo, to Mount Claxelum, there a boundary stone stands; from there downstream to the spring Lebriemelum, there a boundary stone stands; from there along the straight stream Eniseca to the river Porcobera, there a boundary stone stands; from there downstream to the river Porcobera, where the rivers Edus and Porcobera meet, there a boundary stone stands. We judge that land to be public land, and it appears that the castellan Langenses and Veiturios should possess and enjoy it. In return for that land, the Langenses shall pay to the public treasury of Genua 400 victoriate coins annually. If the Langenses do not pay that money or do not provide security to the satisfaction of the Genuates, so that there is no delay on the part of the Genuenses, they may collect that money as they see fit. For the grain and wine harvested in that land, the Langenses shall give to the public treasury of Genua a twentieth part of the grain and a sixth part of the wine annually. For those who possess land within these boundaries, whether a Genuas or a Veiturian, they may possess and cultivate it under the condition that they pay the yearly tax to the Langenses in proportion, just as the other Langenses who possess land in that territory and enjoy it. Furthermore, no one shall possess land in that territory except by the decision of the majority of the Langenses and Veiturians, provided that they do not admit anyone else unless they are a Genuas or a Veiturian for the purpose of cultivation. If anyone among the majority of the Langenses and Veiturians does not comply with this, they shall not possess or enjoy that land. Regarding the common pasture land in that territory, the Genuates and Veiturios shall not be prevented from grazing their livestock there any more than they are in other common pasture land. No one shall forbid it or commit violence, nor shall anyone prevent them from taking wood and building materials from that land and using them. The tax for the first year shall be paid by the Veiturian Langenses to the public treasury of Genua on the first day of January of the second year. They shall not be obliged to pay tax for the produce they have enjoyed before the first day of January. Regarding the meadows which were adjacent to the fen on the date of the consulship of Lucius Caecilius and Quintus Mucius, in the public land possessed by the Vituries, Langenses, Odiates, Dectunines, Cavaturineis, and Mentovines, no one shall allow them to be occupied or grazed by anyone other than the Langenses, Odiates, Dectunines, Cavaturines, and Mentovines, whoever possesses land there, nor shall anyone enjoy them. If the Langenses, Odiates, Dectunines, Cavaturines, or Mentovines wish to introduce and defend other meadows in that land, they may do so, provided that they do not have a larger area of meadows than they had last summer and enjoyed. The Vituries, who have been judged or condemned for injuries against the Genuenses, and any who are imprisoned for these matters, it seems right that all of them be released and freed by the Genuenses. If anyone considers this unjust, they should approach us on the first available day and be freed from all disputes and public honor. Envoys: Moco Meticanius, son of Meticon; Plaucus Pelianio, son of Pelion.
EDCS-20000142.summary: This is a very lengthy legal inscription from 100 BCE, likely in the territory of Genuateis and Veiturios, defining boundaries of public and private land, establishing tax obligations, and resolving disputes between different communities, possibly related to land use and taxation under Roman administration.

EDCS-80200115.summary: This is a funerary dedication by Marcus Valerius Spero, who held the positions of *viir* and *augustalis*.

EDCS-81000085.translation: Dedicated to Apollo. Gaius Cornelius Germanus, son of Gaius, *aedile*, *iivir*, *praefectus fabrum*.
EDCS-81000085.summary: This is a dedication to Apollo by Gaius Cornelius Germanus, who held several local magistracies.

EDCS-81000086.translation: Dedicated to Diana. Lucius Didius Primus, son of Lucius, *aedile*; and Gaius Fabricius [---], son of Lucius, [---].
EDCS-81000086.summary: This is a dedication to Diana, mentioning two individuals, Lucius Didius Primus and Gaius Fabricius, possibly as priests or officials.

EDCS-81000087.translation: To the Divine Emperor Titus Caesar Vespasian Augustus, son of the Divine, Pontifex Maximus, holder of tribunician power for the 10th time, Imperator for the 17th time, Father of the Fatherland, Censor, Consul for the 8th time, by decree of the Senate and People.
EDCS-81000087.summary: This is a public inscription honoring Emperor Vespasian, listing his titles and honors.

EDCS-81000088.translation: To the departed spirits. For Titus Albritius Petronianus, son of Titus, Roman knight, public contractor; and Petronia Maxima, daughter of Gaius, his mother, and his son. He was buried 15 feet in front and 60 feet deep.
EDCS-81000088.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Titus Albritius Petronianus, a Roman knight and contractor, set up by his mother and son.

EDCS-81000089.translation: To the departed spirits. For Taurionis, freedman of the Emperor, an imperial attendant, a registrar from the census office. Severa, his wife, [erected this].
EDCS-81000089.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Taurionis, an imperial freedman and registrar, set up by his wife.

EDCS-81000090.translation: Lucius Ucranius, son of Gaius, from Pedona, soldier of the 10th Praetorian Cohort, served 10 years and 10 months, died aged 30 years and 10 months. Erected by Lucius Aufilenus, son of Lucius, and Sextus, son of Lucius, [---].
EDCS-81000090.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Lucius Ucranius, a soldier in the Praetorian Guard, detailing his service and age at death, with a dedication by his relatives.

EDCS-81000091.translation: Here rests Laurentius the archpresbyter, brother of Lampadius the bishop. He lived about 85 years. He was buried on the 14th day before the Kalends of October, in the year of Manlius Anicius Severinus, a man of consular rank.
EDCS-81000091.summary: This is a funerary inscription for Laurentius, an archpresbyter and brother of a bishop, mentioning his age and burial date within a consular year.
